papers.title: Semantic Processing in Unresponsive Patients With Acute Brain Injury.
papers.abstract: Early prognostication after acute brain injury (ABI) is challenging because behavioral responsiveness may not accurately reflect preserved cognitive function. Neural responses to semantic incongruity can identify language processing despite the absence of overt behavior. We investigated whether bedside EEG could detect semantic processing in unresponsive patients with ABI and whether its presence was associated with long-term outcomes. In this prospective 2-center cohort study, unresponsive adults with ABI admitted to neurologic intensive care units between 2022 and 2025 underwent bedside EEG during a language paradigm comparing congruent and incongruent sentence endings (e.g., "my favorite color is green/soon"). Semantic processing was defined by differential event-related responses within centroparietal channels (300-500 milliseconds) using cluster-based permutation testing with false discovery rate correction. Outcomes were assessed for recovery of consciousness and functional recovery (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score ≥4) at 12 months by blinded interviewers. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and likelihood ratios. Among 105 patients (mean age 58 ± 19 years; 21% women; 53% Hispanic/Latino), the most common etiologies were intracerebral hemorrhage (45%), traumatic brain injury (43%), and subarachnoid hemorrhage (10%). Withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy occurred in 31%. Semantic processing was detected in 13 patients (12%). Recovery of consciousness occurred in 77% of patients with semantic processing compared with 49% without semantic processing (odds ratio [OR] 3.5; 95% CI 0.9-13.5, p = 0.08). Functional recovery occurred in 42% with semantic processing compared with 14% without semantic processing (OR 4.5; 95% CI 1.2-16.6, p = 0.03). Semantic processing was highly specific but insensitive for predicting both recovery of consciousness (specificity 94%, sensitivity 18%) and functional recovery (specificity 92%, sensitivity 29%). After excluding patients who underwent withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy or died of non-neurologic medical complications, specificity increased to 100% for recovery of consciousness and 95% for functional recovery. EEG evidence of semantic processing can be detected in a subset of unresponsive patients with ABI during the acute phase of injury and is associated with favorable long-term outcomes. Semantic processing was a specific but insensitive biomarker of recovery, suggesting potential utility as a rule-in marker of preserved cognitive function. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Investigating pain‑specific sleep disturbances in 3 orofacial pain conditions: Trigeminal neuropathic pain, temporomandibular disorders and orofacial pain presentation of primary headaches.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common in orofacial pain (OFP), yet most studies focus on individual conditions. Whether factors associated with sleep disturbance differ across neuropathic, musculoskeletal, and headache-related OFP remains unclear. To assess demographic, clinical, pain-related, and psychological factors associated with sleep disturbance within each OFP diagnostic category. This cross-sectional study included 333 patients with OFP, predominantly chronic in nature: painful temporomandibular disorders (TMD; n=123), trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP; n=134), and orofacial presentations of primary headache disorders (OFPHD; n=76). Sleep disturbance was assessed using the Chronic Pain Sleep Inventory (CPSI). Associations between sleep disturbance and demographic, clinical, pain-related, and psychological factors were examined using univariate and multivariate analyses. Pain-related functional interference was consistently associated with sleep disturbance across diagnostic groups. Female sex was independently associated with sleep disturbance in TNP, whereas pain intensity and duration were independently associated with sleep disturbance in TMD. Patients with OFPHD reported particularly high levels of pain-related nocturnal awakening. These findings support the assessment of sleep as a core component of OFP management and suggest that subgroup-specific factors should be considered when evaluating and addressing sleep-related problems in this population.
papers.journal: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Neonatal Seizure Detection: A Pragmatic Evaluation of Clinical Performance Tradeoffs in Clinical EEG.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate how three artificial intelligence (AI)-based neonatal seizure detectors (NSDs) perform in a large, clinically acquired data set and their potential to support timely seizure identification. We conducted a secondary analysis of continuous EEG (cEEG) recordings from 169 neonates born at ≥35 weeks gestation with neonatal encephalopathy. Seizure presence was determined by independent review by two or three pediatric encephalographers, and 2,455 individual seizures were annotated by a single expert as a pragmatic, clinically representative reference standard. Three NSDs were evaluated: a feature-based support vector machine detector (NSD1) and two deep-learning detectors (NSD2 and Persyst-15). Using an any-overlap approach, outcomes included neonate-level seizure identification, seizure-level detection, false detections per day (FD/day), and detection latency. We analyzed 15,343 hours of cEEG (median 98 hours per neonate); 55 neonates (33%) had seizures. All NSDs identified ≥95% of neonates with seizures. Seizure-level detection varied: NSD2 detected 35% (IQR 17-53%), NSD1 63% (IQR 38-82%), and Persyst-15 60% (IQR 37-80%) of seizures. NSD1 generated significantly more FDs (46 FD/day, IQR 22-82) than NSD2 (3.2 IQR 1.2-9.3) and Persyst-15 (2.8 IQR 1.1-6.2; P < 0.0001). The median time to first true detection was <1 minute for NSD1 and Persyst-15, versus 26 minutes for NSD2. AI-based NSDs demonstrated high infant-level sensitivity but different tradeoffs between seizure-level detection and alarm burden. These findings highlight how AI tools may augment clinical EEG workflows and support earlier seizure recognition, while underscoring the need for evaluation under real-world conditions to guide safe and effective implementation.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.abstract: Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) is widely used for presurgical evaluation in epilepsy, yet practice patterns vary substantially across centers, contributing to heterogeneity in the literature. We examined differences in SEEG experience, techniques, and complications across Europe and North America centers. An electronic 39-item REDCap survey was distributed to centers participating in the American Stereo-EEG Consortium and EpiCARE Consortium. The survey assessed center characteristics, electrode planning and implantation, monitoring practices, and complications. Sixty-six centers responded, including 38 from North America and 28 from Europe. North American centers more frequently used nurse-led ictal and postictal assessments (16/38 vs. 5/28; P = 0.06) and robotic image-guided implantation systems (37/38 vs. 17/28; P < 0.001), with a trend toward higher case volumes. Compared with European centers, North American programs were less likely to have over 15 years of SEEG experience (6/38 vs. 12/28; P = 0.015), fewer dedicated SEEG readers (12/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.001), and less frequent use of SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation (13/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.01). Symptomatic hemorrhage was more frequently reported among North American centers in the unadjusted analysis (9/38 vs. 1/28; p = 0.035); however, the regional difference was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for center SEEG experience and annual case volume. Significant differences exist between North American and European SEEG practices. North American centers more commonly use robotic implantation and manage higher volume, whereas European centers demonstrate greater experience and more frequent use of SEEG-guided ablation. These findings support the need for standardized protocols to improve safety and outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society

papers.title: Mindfulness-based stress reduction for sleep quality and emotional state in menopause-related insomnia symptoms.
papers.abstract: This study examined the efficacy and safety of mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) for menopause-related insomnia symptoms, with a focus on anxiety, depression, sleep quality, coping styles and quality of life. Eighty-two patients with menopause-related insomnia symptoms were randomized into an experimental group (n = 41, MBSR plus routine health intervention) and a control group (n = 41, routine health intervention) for a 12-week intervention. Emotional state, sleep quality, disease coping styles and quality of life were assessed using standardized scales, with intervention adherence and adverse events recorded as secondary outcomes. Compared with routine care alone, the MBSR group achieved significantly larger decreases in Self-Rating Anxiety Scale and Self-Rating Depression Scale scores, lower Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores, more positive improvements in disease coping styles and more pronounced gains in several quality-of-life dimensions, particularly physical, psychological and social functioning (p < 0.01). The experimental group had high offline and online adherence rates, with no significant between-group differences in adherence (p > 0.05). The adverse event incidence was below 5% in both groups, with no serious adverse events reported. This study confirms that 12-week MBSR is a safe and effective intervention for improving sleep quality, negative emotions, coping styles and quality of life in patients with menopause-related insomnia symptoms.
papers.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society

papers.title: Poor sleep quality and anxiety in patients with diabetes mellitus and its association with glycemic control: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Sleep is crucial for maintaining physical and mental health, and poor sleep quality is associated with an increased risk of metabolic, cognitive, and cardiovascular diseases. This study aimed to assess sleep quality and factors associated with poor sleep quality, such as mental disorders, especially anxiety, in adult patients with type 2 diabetes in Morocco. A cross-sectional study was conducted on patients with type 2 diabetes, using random selection, aged 39-85, in the clinical neurophysiology and internal medicine department of the Mohammed V Military Instruction Hospital, between 30/09/2024 and 30/12/2024. The questionnaire comprised demographic data, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7). Descriptive tests, independent two-sample t-tests, chi-square tests, and logistic regressions were performed using Jamovi version 2.6.2. Out of the 120 participants, the mean age of our patients was 65.4 ± 9.32 years, of whom 66.67% were women. The mean PSQI score was 9.18 ± 3.73, and the mean GAD-7 score was 8.0 ± 6.11. Poor sleep quality was reported in 84.2% of participants, while a binary logistic regression analysis revealed that poor sleep quality was not significantly associated with high HbA1c, but rather was highly significant with age and GAD-7. The study reveals that poor sleep quality is common among type 2 diabetic patients in Morocco, and is strongly associated with generalized anxiety disorders. These findings underscore the crucial role of psychological factors in diabetes management. They highlight the need for a comprehensive and integrated approach that takes into account not only biomedical aspects but also the psychological and behavioral dimensions of patients.

papers.title: Sleep-like slow waves during wakefulness are associated with hallucinations and poorer cognition in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Slow waves during sleep are fundamental for neural homeostasis, metabolic regulation, and waste clearance and are known to be altered in neurodegenerative diseases. Sleep-like slow waves (SLSWs) have been observed in awake, healthy individuals, where they are linked to fluctuations in vigilance and mind-wandering. Whether SLSWs are altered in Parkinson's disease (PD), and whether such alterations contribute to psychiatric or cognitive complications, remains unknown. In a cohort of 84 nondemented patients with PD and 30 healthy older adults, we found that SLSWs occurred more frequently in patients with PD. Hallucinatory traits in patients with PD were associated with higher SLSW amplitude, especially over frontocentral regions. Moreover, more prominent SLSWs were associated with poorer cognitive functions. We conclude that, whereas slow waves during sleep have positive physiological functions, exacerbated diurnal SLSWs may reflect responses related to PD neuropathology, at the cost of hallucinations and reduced cognitive function.

papers.title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury.
papers.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body-irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

papers.title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface.
papers.abstract: In electroencephalography, hair remains a major barrier to electrode-skin contact, limiting signal quality. Here, we introduce electronic hair (eHAIR), a strategy that converts hair into a bioelectronic interface using mixed ionic-electronic conductive polymer dyes. Hair, a keratinized filament anchored within the skin, provides a stable and naturally distributed platform for interfacing. Two complementary approaches based on polythiophene derivatives enable rapid, washable functionalization of hair bundles or semipermanent coating of individual strands. The resulting eHAIR forms conformal, low-impedance interfaces that support electrophysiological recordings with increased signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving the underlying neural dynamics without gels or rigid hardware. Beyond passive sensing, eHAIR-based organic electrochemical transistors enable local signal amplification, with gain defined by hair geometry. By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.

papers.title: FDTest: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem as a test for memory effects in brain dynamics.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in neuroscience is to understand how the brain flexibly balances local and distributed information processing to support diverse cognitive and conscious states. We hypothesize that a key signature of this balance is the presence of memory effects, which arise when a brain region's future activity depends not only on its current state, but also on past information fed back from the wider network. Here we introduce the FDTest, a method for assessing local memory effects in multidimensional systems by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). We first apply this framework to whole-brain models fitted to human neuroimaging data, demonstrating that the brain's memory structure reflects its underlying connectivity. We then extend the analysis to individualized models of subjects during wakefulness and deep sleep. Memory effects are consistently stronger in wakefulness, indicating richer inter-regional dependencies and more integrated dynamics. These findings establish local memory as a dynamical marker of brain state and position the FDTest as a principled tool for probing the hidden structure of neural dynamics.

papers.title: The Skin-Mood Axis in Midlife: Neuro-Immuno-Endocrine Cross-Talk in Perimenopausal and Menopausal Aesthetic Dermatology.
papers.abstract: Perimenopause and menopause may alter skin quality, repair capacity, sleep, mood, self-perception, and aesthetic motivation, yet midlife aesthetic aging is often framed primarily around estrogen and collagen loss. To propose a midlife skin-mood axis that integrates cutaneous biology, neuroendocrine signaling, immune activity, and psychosocial experience in perimenopausal and menopausal aesthetic dermatology. This narrative review synthesizes evidence regarding menopausal hormonal change, barrier and extracellular matrix remodeling, stress and sleep physiology, oxytocin-related signaling, body image, observer perception, and aesthetic motivation. Midlife skin concerns may reflect interactions among reduced barrier resilience, altered repair capacity, neuroendocrine stress pathways, and changes in self-perception rather than isolated tissue aging. These relationships may influence tissue readiness, consultation goals, recovery counseling, patient-reported outcomes, and treatment satisfaction. Recognizing the skin-mood axis may help aesthetic dermatologists individualize consultation, sequence treatments around tissue quality and recovery capacity, and align procedural choices with patient motivation and realistic patient-centered outcomes.
papers.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]

papers.title: Modest loss of sleep increases susceptibility to cybersecurity threats.
papers.abstract: Sleep restriction leads to impaired cognitive processing across domains. I examined whether the transition to daylight saving time (DST), typically accompanied by compromised sleep, would lead to an increase in the probability of falling prey to a simulated phishing attack using a fully naturalistic experiment with random assignment and blinding. A predatory email was sent to employees at the University of California, Irvine (N = 11,218) either on the morning of Monday following the transition to DST or one week earlier. The transition led to a ~13% increase in the probability of clicking a suspicious link, without affecting the probability of opening the email or reporting it as spam. These results demonstrate that even modest, mundane, and acute loss of sleep has real-life, potentially hazardous, implications for cognitive function.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits.
papers.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway-molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Sleep starts: Phenomenology and associations with sleep, psychological, and demographic characteristics.
papers.abstract: Sleep starts (SS) are transient phenomena during sleep onset. Although traditionally characterized by sudden muscle jerks, they may also involve sensory, cognitive, emotional, and autonomic experiences. Despite their high prevalence, empirical data on phenomenology and associated characteristics remain limited. This online survey examined SS phenomenology and exploratory associations with demographic, sleep-related, and psychological variables in 194 adults. Participants with self-reported sleep-related movement disorders or relevant medical conditions were excluded. Individuals reporting abrupt awakenings ≥1/week and ≥1 additional symptom formed the SS group (SS frequency ≥1, n = 96); all others the comparison group (SS frequency <1, n = 98). Because SS were operationalized using self-reported symptoms, they could not be distinguished from related sleep-onset phenomena (e.g., exploding head syndrome, hypnagogic hallucinations). Standardized questionnaires (PSQI, ISI, ESS, MZS, HADS) assessed sleep quality, insomnia severity, daytime sleepiness, dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and anxiety/depression symptoms. Participants described diverse experiences including motor jerks, falling sensations, dream-like experiences, somatosensory symptoms, autonomic arousal, and emotional reactions, accompanied by alarm, anxiety, and confusion. Compared with controls, the SS group reported poorer sleep quality, greater insomnia severity, stronger dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and higher anxiety/depressive symptoms (all p < .05). Exploratory regression analyses indicated that poorer sleep quality, stronger dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and higher anxiety symptoms were associated with higher SS frequency, whereas depressive symptoms were not. The final model explained 26.9% of variance (R2 = .269, adjusted R2 = .245). More frequent SS were retrospectively reported during emotional stress, whereas sleep deprivation was perceived as less influential. Although many described SS as manageable, a substantial subgroup reported distress and sleep disruption. This suggests that SS represent heterogeneous sleep-onset experiences associated with subjective sleep disturbance and cognitive-emotional arousal. Although causality cannot be inferred from cross-sectional self-report data, the results highlight potentially relevant links between SS and sleep-related cognitive-emotional processes.

papers.title: Piloting cannabis for sleep disturbance in palliative care over 5 weeks: The pillow study protocol.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance affects 60% of cancer patients, 3-fold that of the general population, and is frequently driven by clinical characteristics, physical symptoms, and psychological distress. Sleep disturbance and other symptoms often exacerbate one another, leading to reduced health-related quality of life (HRQOL). Sleep is the most commonly reported reason for cannabis use among adults with cancer, yet clinical evidence supporting its use for symptom management remains limited. This report describes a protocol for a pilot randomized trial designed to evaluate the safety and feasibility of a cannabis-based intervention and to explore its preliminary efficacy for sleep disturbance and HRQOL. This pilot parallel-arm randomized clinical trial will enroll 50 patients from the Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center (OSUCCC; anticipated Fall 2026). Eligible participants will be new to the OSUCCC's Palliative Care clinic and report at least moderate sleep disturbance. Participants will be randomized by sex and race strata to receive either usual care or a nightly oral cannabis gummy containing 5 mg Δ-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and 5 mg cannabidiol (CBD), taken 1 hour before bedtime for 30 days. Adverse events will be monitored throughout the study. Sleep, HRQOL, and related symptoms will be assessed using self-reported questionnaires, ecological momentary assessments, and actigraphy. Findings will provide critical safety, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy data to support a future large-scale, multisite trial targeting sleep disturbance and symptom palliation in cancer care.

papers.title: HRA-Former: Hierarchical Region-Aware Transformer with Structure-Preserving Multi-Stage Learning for EEG-Based Driver Fatigue Detection.
papers.abstract: Driver fatigue is associated with changes in neural rhythms and interregional coordination. However, most EEG-based fatigue detection methods model dense inter-electrode dependencies with limited attention to the electrode-to-region hierarchy. Conventional classification objectives may also favor discriminative patterns while inadequately preserving EEG spatial and spectral structure. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hierarchical region-aware Transformer with structure-preserving multi-stage learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection. The proposed framework first aggregates electrode-level features into region-level features using prototypeattention aggregation and incorporates two-dimensional scalp positional encoding to retain spatial topology. A region-aware attention mask regulates information propagation based on predefined region assignments, preserving electrode-to-region interactions and global communication among regions. Furthermore, a two-stage learning strategy is developed. In the first stage, masked EEG feature reconstruction and fatigue classification are jointly optimized to learn structure-preserving and taskrelevant representations. In the second stage, the pretrained encoder is transferred to a dedicated classifier for supervised fatigue recognition. Experiments on SEED-VIG and an independently collected dataset achieved subject-dependent accuracies of 95.18% and 86.67%, respectively, outperforming representative methods. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. These results suggest that electrode-toregion modeling enables physiologically structured EEG representations and improves fatigue detection.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: A Neuroscientific Prior-Guided Multi-View Network With Structured Channel Selection for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition is important for affective human-computer interaction and computer-aided mental health monitoring. Existing deep learning methods often overlook brain spatial topology or rely on complex dynamic graphs, which may introduce volume-conduction-induced spurious correlations and limit interpretability. This paper proposes SGA-MVTN, a neuroscientific prior-guided two-stage framework integrating a Multi-View Tower Network (MVTN) for prior-constrained feature modeling and a Structured Genetic Algorithm (SGA) for topology-aware channel selection. Specifically, MVTN keeps anatomically defined spatial views and frequency-band-specific spectral views separate until fusion, while SGA embeds functional grouping and hemispheric symmetry priors into evolutionary operators. Unlike spatial-spectral models operating on a fixed electrode set, the proposed framework connects view-specific representation learning with topology-aware electrode subset search. Under the leave-one-subject-out protocol, full-channel MVTN achieves 87.91% on SEED and 71.09% on SEED-IV. Under the channel-selection protocol, SGA-MVTN reduces the number of EEG channels by 54.84% while retaining 95.56% of the corresponding full-channel accuracy and achieves the highest accuracy among the evaluated reduced-channel methods. The separate towers also provide model-derived spatial and spectral importance estimates.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Model based Federated Learning Framework for Seizure-Type Classification.
papers.abstract: Accurate seizure-type identification is of great significance for epilepsy patient treatment and management. Manual electroencephalogram (EEG) data analysis, the traditional method, is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and subjective. While deep learning has shown great potential in medical diagnosis, it faces privacy and data silo challenges in handling multi-center EEG data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-branch model and federated learning-based automatic classification method for seizure types. A federated learning framework is introduced to facilitate multi-center data collaborative training while protecting data privacy. In the base model, the one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1DCNN) and the two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2DCNN) are integrated to extract the complexity features of EEG signals and the topological features of brain networks, respectively, and the dual-modal features are adaptively integrated through the dynamic attention fusion module. In local training of federated learning framework, the FedProx optimization strategy is adopted to effectively solve the model update divergence problem caused by non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data and improve the model generalization ability. Experimental results show that the proposed federated learning framework performs well in core indicators of seizure-type classification such as accuracy and macro-average F1 score. Even in the case of extremely unbalanced data, the proposed method can still maintain an accuracy of 98.42% and a macro-average F1 score of 94.79%. This method provides an effective solution for distributed medical data collaborative training, which is of great significance for promoting the accurate diagnosis and treatment of epilepsy.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: Upper-Extremity Neuropathies Secondary to Prolonged Decubitus Positioning.
papers.abstract: Upper-extremity nerve palsies secondary to prolonged decubitus positioning represent a spectrum of nerve injuries, with outcomes that range in severity from transient conduction block to irreversible functional impairment. These neuropathies occur when a loss of protective sensory feedback and/or muscle tone is combined with an inability to reposition the extremity, allowing for sustained nerve compression or stretch beyond the threshold for injury. Commonly injured structures include the radial nerve, median nerve, ulnar nerve, and the brachial plexus. These structures have unique anatomical vulnerabilities and mechanisms of injury related to prolonged decubitus positioning. Scenarios in which these injuries can occur include prolonged immobilization because of sleep, intoxication with drugs or alcohol, and anesthesia in the setting of surgery or mechanical ventilation for critically ill patients. The purpose of this review is to synthesize current evidence related to the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of these injuries.

papers.title: Examining the Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of a Health App for Postacute Pandemic Years in Managing Physical and Psychological Distress Symptoms: Pilot Quasi-Experimental Study.
papers.abstract: Physical and psychological distress symptoms can adversely affect daily functioning and quality of life, highlighting the need for accessible self-management support. Although mobile health (mHealth) interventions show promise in supporting physical symptom management, evidence regarding their feasibility and potential effects on psychological distress remains limited. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of the health app for postacute pandemic years (HAPPY) for managing physical and psychological distress symptoms. A 2-arm, single-blind, quasi-experimental trial was conducted from July 2023 to January 2024. Thirty-eight participants experiencing distress symptoms related to COVID-19 were assigned to the experimental group or a waitlist control group. The experimental group received a 24-week mHealth intervention through the HAPPY app, which included an 8-week supervised phase with weekly face-to-face sessions and a 16-week self-management phase. The control group received no active treatment. Feasibility was assessed through recruitment, adherence, and adverse event monitoring, whereas preliminary efficacy was evaluated at 8 weeks (T1) and 24 weeks (T2) and compared with baseline (T0) using quantitative measures of distress, fatigue, sleep quality, pain, emotional regulation, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The study demonstrated the feasibility of the HAPPY app, with a recruitment rate of 88.37% (38/43), a dropout rate of 10.5% (4/38), and an adherence rate of 93.33% (14/15) for the supervised sessions. No adverse events were reported. Significant within-group improvements were observed for distress (Kessler Psychological Distress Scale [K10]; P<.001), fatigue (Brief Fatigue Inventory-Chinese [BFI-C]; P<.001), sleep quality (Chinese Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [CPSQI]; P=.009), and PTSD symptoms (Chinese Impact of Event Scale-Revised [CIES-R]; P=.02). However, between-group differences were limited. The study demonstrated the HAPPY app's feasibility, acceptability, and potential efficacy for managing physical and psychological distress symptoms. High recruitment, retention, and adherence rates, along with measurable improvements in distress, fatigue, sleep quality, and pain, suggest the app's promise as a scalable intervention. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05459896; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05459896.

papers.title: Impacts of Tonsillectomy on Growth Trajectories in Children.
papers.abstract: To characterize long-term growth trajectories after tonsillectomy and examine whether they differed according to preoperative body size. This retrospective cohort study included 117 children aged 5-9 years who underwent tonsillectomy between 2008 and 2020. Longitudinal BMI, weight, and height z score were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Baseline BMI z score was modeled continuously, with adjustment for baseline age, sex, and tonsil size. Primary analyses included Years 1 through 5. Lower baseline BMI z score was associated with a greater increase in BMI z score from preoperative assessment to Year 1. Little change or a modest decrease was estimated at higher baseline values. For each 1-unit higher baseline BMI z score, the estimated preoperative-to-Year 1 change was 0.206 smaller (β = -0.206; 95% CI, -0.319 to -0.094; p < 0.001), reaching zero at approximately +1.0. However, the overall baseline BMI z score-by-postoperative year interaction was not significant (p = 0.817), indicating no difference in BMI trajectory shape during Years 1 through 5 by baseline BMI z score. Weight z score showed a similar pattern, whereas height z score showed less variation. Overall interactions were nonsignificant for weight (p = 0.541) and height (p = 0.119). Lower preoperative BMI z score was associated with greater early postoperative increases in BMI z score, whereas little change or a modest decrease was estimated at higher baseline values during postoperative Year 1. Thereafter, changes during Years 1 through 5 did not differ significantly by baseline BMI z score. 4 (Retrospective cohort study).

papers.title: Rapidly progressive sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease overshadowed by a grief reaction and parkinsonism: a case report.
papers.abstract: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (sCJD) is a rapidly progressive and invariably fatal prion disease in which the first manifestations are psychiatric in a substantial proportion of cases. We report a 60-year-old man in whom sCJD was overshadowed both by a grief reaction and by a years-long presumed diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. Depressive, psychotic and cognitive symptoms that emerged after the loss of a close relative were initially interpreted as reactive, and an unexpected clinical deterioration followed the introduction of antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment. Electroencephalography showed periodic triphasic activity over the right frontotemporoparietal region, and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated widespread bilateral diffusion restriction in cortical and deep grey matter. Autoimmune and paraneoplastic panels were negative, and a positive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) assay established a diagnosis of probable sCJD. The case underlines the importance of an organic differential diagnosis and of early multidisciplinary assessment in late-onset, rapidly progressive psychiatric presentations.
papers.journal: Neuropsychiatrie : Klinik, Diagnostik, Therapie und Rehabilitation : Organ der Gesellschaft Osterreichischer Nervenarzte und Psychiater

papers.title: Effects on Sleep Quality and Bioelectrical Parameters of Cellular Health After Administration of a Plant Protein Supplement Combined with Ashwagandha and Rhodiola: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances affect a significant portion of the global population, impacting health and quality of life. While plant-based proteins and adaptogens such as ashwagandha and rhodiola have shown individual benefits, their combined effects remain poorly understood. This study evaluated whether a nutritional intervention combining plant protein with ashwagandha-rhodiola could improve sleep quality in middle-aged adults. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted with 100 participants aged 35-70 years, assigned to VERUM (n=50) or PLACEBO (n=50) groups. The VERUM group received plant protein (27 g/day: pea, rice, hemp isolate) plus adaptogen tablets (Rhodiola rosea 300 mg + Withania somnifera KSM-66® 500 mg) for 30 days. Sleep quality was assessed using the validated Sleep Quality Questionnaire (SQQ) completed daily. Phase angle was measured by bioimpedance (BIA-TELELAB) pre- and post-intervention. Data were analyzed using longitudinal mixed models and non-parametric tests. Seventy-seven participants completed bioimpedance analysis (VERUM group; n= 38, PLACEBO group n=39; mean age 47.8±8.2 years), and sixty-one completed sleep assessments (VERUM group n=32; PLACEBO group n=29). The VERUM group showed highly significant improvements: sleep difficulty reduced by 56% (p<0.001, d=0.91), daytime sleepiness decreased by 60% (p<0.001, d=0.85), and total sleep score improved by 58% (p<0.001, d=0.96), representing a 3.7-fold greater improvement than placebo. Phase angle changes were minimal in both groups. No adverse events were reported. The combination of plant protein with ashwagandha-rhodiola for 30 days produces substantial, clinically relevant improvements in sleep quality with an excellent safety profile, with statistically greater improvements compared to placebo.
papers.journal: Plant foods for human nutrition (Dordrecht, Netherlands)

papers.title: Is there an association between awake and sleep bruxism? : a meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: To systematically review and meta-analyze the association between sleep bruxism (SB) and awake bruxism (AB) in children and adults. Observational studies evaluating the association between SB and AB were included. Studies were classified as direct or indirect evidence and according to diagnostic certainty as subject-, clinically-, and device-based. Random effects meta-analyses were performed using odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Forty-nine studies were included. Most were cross sectional (n = 41), followed by case control studies (n = 6) and cohort studies (n = 2). Twenty-four studies were classified as direct evidence and twenty-five as indirect evidence. Most studies assessed subject-based bruxism (n = 35), followed by clinically-based bruxism (n = 10), mixed diagnostic criteria (n = 3), and device-based bruxism (n = 1). The overall meta-analysis included 8970 participants in the SB group and 25,730 in the AB group, showing a significant association between both conditions (OR = 3.74; 95% CI: 2.47; 5.67). The association remained significant in adults, children, direct studies, indirect studies, and studies assessing subject-based or clinically-based bruxism. Heterogeneity was high across all analyses. Current evidence indicates a significant positive association between sleep bruxism and awake bruxism. However, the predominance of cross-sectional designs, self-reported diagnostic methods, and high heterogeneity limits causal interpretation. SB and AB should not be assessed as completely isolated clinical findings. This meta-analysis shows that individuals with SB have higher odds of presenting AB. Therefore, when one circadian manifestation is identified, clinicians should actively investigate the other, particularly in patients with temporomandibular disorders, orofacial pain, sleep complaints, or stress related symptoms.

papers.title: Undiagnosed poor sleep quality is common among older adults with type 2 diabetes and is associated with impaired quality of life and depressive symptoms.
papers.abstract: Although diabetes is linked to sleep disorders that can reduce quality of life (QOL) and increase depression risk, these conditions are still rarely assessed in clinical practice. This study aimed to evaluate sleep quality in older adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and its association with QOL and depressive symptoms. 151 individuals with T2D aged > 60 years without known sleep disorders underwent a review of clinical history and therapy, biochemical exams, and assessment of Pittsburgh Sleep Quality index (PSQI), World Health Organization QOL Bref (WHOQOL-BREF) scale, and Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). The population was then split into: Good Sleepers (PSQI ≤ 5) and Poor Sleepers (PSQI > 5). The prevalence of low sleep quality was 63.6%. Poor Sleepers showed numerically comparable age, sex, body mass index, diabetes duration, and glycaemic control with Good Sleepers. However, Poor Sleepers showed lower scores in the physical health and psychological health domains of WHOQOL-BREF. After adjusting for confounders, PSQI score was associated with CVD (β = 0.26, P = 0.008) and diabetes duration (β = 0.24, P = 0.022). Furthermore, the scores in the physical health (β=-0.35) as well as the psychological health (β =-0.31) domains of the WHOQOL-BREF and the GDS (β = 0.24) were all independently associated with PSQI score (all P < 0.05). In our population of older adults with T2D, poor sleep quality was highly prevalent and associated with poor quality of life and depressive symptoms. Thus, sleep quality assessment should be carefully considered in clinical practice, especially in people with long diabetes duration and complications.

papers.title: Energy drink consumption and associated lifestyle factors among German adolescents: findings from the EDKAR-study.
papers.abstract: The consumption of energy drinks (EDs) has become increasingly popular among adolescents. The present study aimed to comprehensively characterize ED consumption behavior and associated lifestyle factors in pupils aged 15-18 years. The cross-sectional EDKAR-study assessed data from 5100 German pupils using an online questionnaire. Following exclusion criteria, 4893 pupils were categorized into six ED consumer groups based on the frequency, duration, and quantity of their reported ED consumption: non-consumers, occasional, moderate, regular, chronic low, and chronic high consumers. Overall, 65.6% (n = 3208) reported ED consumption within the past 12 months, 12.6% on ≥ 4 days per week, and 3.9% daily. Median (IQR) daily ED intake was higher in groups with more frequent ED consumption, ranging from 20.5 ml/day (5.3-41.0) among occasional consumers to 818 ml/day (571-1250) among chronic high consumers. Reported adverse effects likewise increased from occasional to chronic high consumers, ranging from 23.2% to 50.2%, with palpitations, poor sleep, headaches, and chest pressure reported most frequently. Harmful lifestyle behaviors also increased from non-consumers to chronic high consumers, including alcohol intake (from 0.2 to 2.3 glasses per week), smoking rates (from 5.6% to 53.3%; cannabis: from 10.3% to 48.8%), short sleep duration (< 5 h/night on weekdays: from 4.7% to 20.6%), and excessive daily screen time (> 8 h/day: from 35.8% to 72.8%). The EDKAR-study highlights the high prevalence of ED consumption among German adolescents and its association with several harmful lifestyle behaviors, underscoring the importance of raising awareness of potential adverse health effects of ED consumption.

papers.title: Systemic sarcoidosis with neurosarcoidosis presenting with pulmonary embolism, epileptic seizures, and neuropsychiatric involvement in a patient with pre-existing schizophrenia: a diagnostic challenge.
papers.abstract: Neurosarcoidosis affects approximately 5-10% of patients with systemic sarcoidosis and may mimic primary psychiatric disease, delaying diagnosis. We report a 52-year-old man with pre-existing schizophrenia admitted with bilateral pulmonary embolism and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Systemic sarcoidosis was confirmed by endobronchial ultrasound-guided lymph node biopsy and gastric histology. The patient subsequently developed epileptic seizures and a progressive neuropsychiatric syndrome initially attributed to his known psychiatric disorder. Electroencephalography demonstrated diffuse slowing with abundant epileptiform discharges and electro-clinical seizures of left temporal onset; brain MRI showed leptomeningeal involvement with cortical diffusion restriction; cerebrospinal fluid excluded infectious causes and showed an intrathecal immune response. A diagnosis of probable neurosarcoidosis was established, although a seizure-related contribution to the MRI findings could not be excluded. Treatment with high-dose corticosteroids and antiseizure medication was followed by marked clinical improvement and reported resolution of the MRI abnormalities. This case underscores the importance of considering neurosarcoidosis in patients with systemic granulomatous disease who develop new neuropsychiatric symptoms, even when a pre-existing psychiatric diagnosis offers an apparently sufficient explanation.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of selective orexin 2 receptor agonists in narcolepsy type 1: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Selective orexin 2 receptor (OX2R) agonists target the orexin deficiency underlying narcolepsy type 1, but their efficacy and safety across compounds have not been quantitatively synthesized. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane library from inception through September 10, 2026, for randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of oral OX2R agonists in narcolepsy type 1.The primary outcomes were Maintenance of Wakefulness Test sleep latency, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, and weekly cataplexy rate. Safety analyses included all double-blind active regimens. Adjusted mean differences and incidence rate ratios were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Evidence certainty was assessed using GRADE. Five trials randomized 550 participants and evaluated TAK-994, oveporexton, or alixorexton over 6-12 weeks; the primary efficacy synthesis included 337 participants. Compared with placebo, OX2R agonists increased Maintenance of Wakefulness Test sleep latency by 22.7 min (95% CI 16.8-28.7; 95% prediction interval, 8.0-37.4; I2 = 74.4%; low-certainty evidence), reduced epworth sleepiness scale scores (mean difference, - 9.8 points; 95% CI - 10.9 to - 8.8; I2 = 0%; moderate-certainty evidence), and reduced weekly cataplexy rates by 69% (incidence rate ratio, 0.31; 95% CI 0.23-0.41; I2 = 0%; moderate-certainty evidence). Urinary frequency, insomnia, urinary urgency, and salivary hypersecretion were more frequent with treatment. The TAK-994 program was terminated after hepatotoxicity. Short-term OX2R agonist therapy improved wakefulness, sleepiness, and cataplexy in narcolepsy type 1. Limited trials, substantial MWT heterogeneity, and short follow-up constrain class-wide and long-term safety conclusions.

papers.title: Compassion-Focused Implementation of Smartwatches in Acute Mental Health Care: Mixed Method Replicated Single-Case Study.
papers.abstract: Smartwatches can support mental health care by providing insights into activity and sleep, which are closely linked to mental health and daily functioning. However, their implementation in mental health care practice remains limited. Professionals can feel resistance toward digital mental health interventions if they feel their use is not aligned with therapeutic values, and report a need for guidance on how to use technologies in ways that do align with such values. Compassion, a core value in mental health care, may offer a meaningful frame for implementation. Therefore, we previously co-designed compassion-focused implementation materials: a card set offering practical suggestions of how smartwatch data can support group treatments in ways that counter the self-optimization logic of commercial devices and instead align with compassion. The current study evaluated the compassion-focused card set in practice, to explore whether the introduction of the card set influenced the use of smartwatches in treatment sessions, and mental health professionals' experienced compassion when working with smartwatches, the therapeutic alliance, and acceptance of smartwatches. The card set was evaluated in a mixed methods replicated single-case design with 5 social psychiatric nurses from an acute mental health care team. Data collection included pre- and post-questionnaires, repeated measures, a focus group, and interviews. For smartwatch use, no significant intervention effects were found, though several participants did report the start or increase of use of the smartwatch in sessions during the intervention phase. For compassion, only P2 showed a significant effect of the intervention on experienced compassion when using smartwatches (Tau-U=0.53, 95% CI -0.11 to 0.86; P=.02). This participant reported that the card set helped to make the use of smartwatches more concrete and insightful. For therapeutic alliance and acceptance of the smartwatches, no intervention effects were found. These scores were rather stable over time for most participants. The card set was experienced as flexible and easy to use, supporting session structure and enabling more in-depth, compassionate conversations. At the same time, barriers to sustained smartwatch integration included low patient uptake, challenges in mixed groups in which only some patients wore the smartwatch, and varying digital affinity among professionals. These findings suggest that compassion-focused materials may trigger initial adoption and help reframe smartwatch use in line with therapeutic values. Broader implementation strategies, including further training and tailoring to patient readiness, are required for sustainable integration.

papers.title: Anthropometric indicators and risk of obstructive sleep apnea: Role of HDL-C as a potential mediator.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from 9068 U.S. adults (weighted n = 170.2 million) in the 2015-2020 NHANES. It aimed to elucidate the nonlinear relationships between six anthropometric indices - Relative Fat Mass Index (RFM), Body Roundness Index (BRI), Weight-adjusted Waist Index (WWI), Body Mass Index (BMI), and waist circumference - and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) risk. Furthermore, we pioneered an exploration of the potential mediating role of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). Multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical confounders, revealed significant positive trends between all indices and OSA risk (P for trend < .05). Threshold effect models and smooth curve fitting identified distinct association patterns. RFM exhibited a linear dose-response relationship with OSA (P < .05), whereas BRI, WWI, BMI, and waist circumference demonstrated nonlinear positive correlations with identifiable inflection points (P < .05). Bootstrap mediation analysis (1000 replications) yielded results consistent with a significant mediating role for HDL-C, which explained 5.6 to 21.9% of the observed associations. This effect was most pronounced for WWI (13.2%). Stratified analyses indicated enhanced associations in participants aged < 60 years (interaction P < .05). These findings establish RFM as a linear predictor of OSA, contrasting with the nonlinear dynamics of other adiposity indices. The partial mediation by HDL-C underscores dysregulated lipid metabolism as a key pathological mechanism linking obesity to OSA, supporting the integration of anthropometric screening with lipid profiling to optimize clinical risk stratification and early intervention strategies.

papers.title: The efficacy and safety of olanzapine combined with repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in patients with comorbid anxiety-depression and sleep disorders.
papers.abstract: This retrospective study non-randomized cohort study evaluated the efficacy and safety of adjunctive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with olanzapine in adults with comorbid anxiety-depression and sleep disorders treated between April 2019 and March 2025. A total of 210 patients were included and allocated, according to the treatment actually received in routine clinical practice, to an olanzapine monotherapy group (n = 102) or a combined treatment group receiving olanzapine plus rTMS for 4 weeks (n = 108). Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, including baseline sleep, anxiety, and depression severity, were comparable between groups. After 4 weeks, actigraphy-derived sleep parameters favored the combined group, including higher sleep efficiency (80.31% ± 9.85% vs 76.85% ± 10.53%), longer total sleep time (404.26 ± 14.52 vs 398.26 ± 13.52 minutes), and fewer nighttime awakenings (3.78 ± 0.94 vs 4.12 ± 0.85). Consistent with these objective findings, greater reductions were observed in patient-reported sleep scales, with lower posttreatment Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (8.49 ± 1.24 vs 9.05 ± 1.27) and ISI scores (11.47 ± 1.28 vs 11.91 ± 1.31). Both groups demonstrated improvement in mood and anxiety symptoms; however, reductions in Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (13.51 ± 1.85 vs 14.12 ± 1.49) and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale scores (12.61 ± 1.78 vs 13.37 ± 1.69) were greater with combined therapy, accompanied by higher overall clinical efficacy and improved World Health Organization Quality of Life - Brief Version physical and psychological domains. Metabolic indices (body mass index, fasting blood glucose, and lipids) were similar between groups at baseline and follow-up. Headache occurred more frequently with rTMS, whereas other adverse events were infrequent and comparable. These findings support the short-term effectiveness of olanzapine plus rTMS for improving sleep and affective symptoms without additional metabolic burden. However, the retrospective non-randomized design, potential residual confounding, and 4-week follow-up require cautious interpretation and confirmation in randomized long-term studies.

papers.title: The role of linerixibat in treating pruritus in primary biliary cholangitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Cholestatic pruritus affects up to 89% of patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) and responds poorly to conventional treatment. Linerixibat, an oral ileal bile acid transporter inhibitor, was approved by the Food and Drug Administration in March 2026 as the first medicine indicated specifically for cholestatic-pruritus in PBC. This meta-analysis evaluated its efficacy, safety and pharmacodynamic effects. PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, the Cochrane Library and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to April 2026 for randomized, placebo-controlled trials of linerixibat in adults with PBC and cholestatic pruritus. To avoid unit-of-analysis error, only period 1 data were used from the phase 2a crossover trial, and the shared placebo group of the multi-arm phase 2b trial was divided proportionally across active arms. Random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) models generated mean differences (MD), standardized mean differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals. Certainty was rated using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (PROSPERO CRD420261381897). Three trials randomizing 407 participants were included. Linerixibat reduced Worst Itch Numerical Rating Scale (WI-NRS) score versus placebo (MD -0.71; 95% confidence interval: -1.12 to -0.30; P = .0007; I2 = 0%), below the 2 to 3 point minimal clinically important difference. Sleep interference improved modestly (MD -0.47; P = .04). Responder rates were not significant at ≥2 points (RR 1.06; P = .49), borderline at ≥3 points (RR 1.25; P = .05), and nonsignificant at ≥4 points (RR 1.23; P = .10). Neither the PBC-40 itch domain (P = .14) nor 5-D Itch Scale (P = .28) differed significantly. Target engagement was confirmed by reduced total serum bile acids (P = .003) and fibroblast growth factor 19 (P = .0005) and increased 7α-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one (P < .00001); autotaxin was unchanged (standardized mean difference -0.20; P = .27). Overall adverse events were not significantly increased (RR 1.38; P = .06), but discontinuation (RR 2.75; P = .009), diarrhea (RR 3.69), abdominal pain (RR 2.80) and dyspepsia (RR 7.22) were significantly more frequent with linerixibat. Results at the licensed 40 mg twice-daily dose were concordant (WI-NRS MD -0.75; P = .003). Linerixibat produces a statistically significant but modest reduction in itch intensity below the accepted minimal clinically important difference, alongside a substantial gastrointestinal tolerability burden and roughly 3-fold increase in discontinuation. It is a mechanistically validated, licensed option for refractory cholestatic pruritus, but benefit-harm trade-offs should be discussed explicitly with patients. Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations certainty was moderate for the primary outcome.

papers.title: Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome in an elderly female: A video-based case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome (OMAS) is rare in adults. Here, we report a rare case of OMAS in an elderly patient, accompanied by video documentation and a comprehensive literature review, which may offer valuable insights into the clinical features, diagnosis, and management of this condition. An 81-year-old female was admitted with limb tremors lasting for 1 day. During the hospitalization, she developed opsoclonus, myoclonus, ataxia, behavioral changes, and sleep disturbances. Laboratory and imaging findings were unremarkable, with no tumor detected during follow-up, supporting a diagnosis of idiopathic OMAS. Immunotherapy consisted of steroids, while symptomatic treatment included clonazepam and gabapentin. The patient showed marked symptomatic improvement after immunotherapy. At two-year follow-up, there was no evidence of recurrence or malignancy. In elderly patients, OMAS is extremely rare and often diagnosed and treated late. Comprehensive screening for malignancies and infectious triggers is critical. Early recognition and prompt immunotherapy improve outcomes.

papers.title: Allelo-Labdane Diterpenoids from Abies fabri Targeting CYP707A2 to Inhibit Arabidopsis Seed Germination.
papers.abstract: Gymnosperm plants are rich in allelochemicals that can be used as ideal eco-friendly alternatives to chemical herbicides. Petroleum ether and ethyl acetate crude extracts from the leaves of Abies fabri (Mast.) Craib (Pinaceae) inhibited seed germination of Arabidopsis thaliana. Twenty-four terpenoids were isolated and identified by chromatographic separation and NMR spectral analysis. Compounds 7 and 14-17 showed germination inhibitory activity, among which 7, namely 13-epitorreferol, was selected for mechanistic investigation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were mainly enriched in stress response and plant hormone signaling, especially abscisic acid (ABA) pathways. The results of the in vitro enzyme activity assay and mutant phenotypic analysis indicated that CYP707A2 (ABA 8'-hydroxylase) was one of the targets mediating the inhibitory activity of 7 on seed germination. This work expands allelochemical resources, offering a tool for investigating ABA signaling and providing leads for the development of eco-friendly herbicides.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Assessing Response to Difelikefalin in Adults Receiving Haemodialysis: A Multidisciplinary, Person-Centred Framework for Chronic Kidney Disease-Associated Pruritus.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus remains under-recognised in adults receiving haemodialysis and is associated with impaired sleep, quality of life and daily functioning. Translating treatment effects into consistent routine monitoring remains challenging. To synthesise evidence relevant to multidimensional assessment of response to difelikefalin and propose a practical, person-centred framework for haemodialysis care. State-of-the-art narrative review informed by a structured pragmatic literature search. Not applicable. Evidence was synthesised across itch intensity, sleep-related disruption, pruritus-related quality of life, wider symptom burden, patient-reported outcome measures, implementation in kidney care and exploratory biomarkers. Evidence supports improvements with difelikefalin in itch intensity, sleep-related disruption and pruritus-related quality of life. We propose a brief core set combining the Worst Itching Intensity Numerical Rating Scale with sleep and daily-burden questions, supplemented by Skindex-10 and 5-D Itch when indicated. The combined set, brief burden questions and within-session assessment timing are unvalidated implementation proposals. Full response, partial response and persistent burden are pragmatic communication labels, not validated phenotypes. Reviews around Weeks 4 and 12 are informed by trial assessment points; subsequent 8- to 12-week intervals are pragmatic and unvalidated. Established instrument thresholds support interpretation of change, while exploratory biomarkers remain research-only. The proposed person-centred framework may support multidimensional assessment of difelikefalin response. Its feasibility, response categories and clinical utility require prospective validation before it can be considered a validated clinical pathway.

papers.title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.
papers.abstract: Aeromedical certification is based on a safety-first principle: a pilot or other aircrew member must not have a medical disorder that creates an unacceptable risk of sudden or subtle incapacitation during flight. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the most important determinants of flight fitness, as it may impair consciousness, judgment, rhythm stability, exercise capacity, and hemodynamic reserve. Modern aeromedical decision-making therefore requires the integration of aviation law, operational risk, contemporary cardiology guidelines, advanced imaging, biomarkers, and long-term surveillance. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 1 provides the global licensing framework; the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Part-MED, together with its Acceptable Means of Compliance and Guidance Material, defines detailed operational standards in Europe; and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employs a protocol- and special issuance-based system for many cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This review summarizes the aeromedical assessment of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic and acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cardiomy-opathies, arrhythmias and conduction disorders, pacemakers and implantable cardiac devices, valvular heart disease, aortic disease, congenital heart disease, venous throm-boembolism, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and major respiratory conditions rel-evant to flight certification. The manuscript is aligned with current European Society of Cardiology cardiovascular guidance and with the operational aeromedical principles applied by ICAO, EASA, FAA, and the Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. In general, preserved ventricular function, absence of significant symptoms, low thrombo-embolic and arrhythmic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity support certification or restricted certification. In contrast, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable diabetes, significant residual myocardial ischemia, reduced ejection fraction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, implantable defibrillator therapy, severe valvular disease, significant aortic pathology, major congenital hemodynamic lesions, or poorly controlled sleep apnea usually preclude certification. Final decisions remain individualized and depend on license class, operational role, treatment burden, surveillance data, and the judgment of the aeromedical authority.

papers.title: Manganese Toxicity Observed in Workers at a Ferromanganese Plant.
papers.abstract: We evaluated 11 male workers with elevated serum manganese levels and T1 hyperintensities in the globus pallidus, features of manganese toxicity, all of whom were employed at a single ferromanganese plant. They exhibited clinical features of manganism, including behavioral issues, forgetfulness, headache, decreased sleep, generalized weakness, tingling and stretching sensations in the limbs, hand and jaw tremors, dysarthria, hypophonia, rapid speech, rigidity, difficulty in walking, and falls. Positron emission tomography scans performed on two patients showed presynaptic dopaminergic deficits. All patients ceased working in the environment and experienced partial improvement with levodopa therapy.
papers.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology

papers.title: Acute intermittent carotid body stimulations induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling in rats.
papers.abstract: Hypertension, the leading modifiable risk factor for global mortality, is driven in >50% of cases by neurogenic mechanisms linked to heightened sympathetic nerve activity (SNA). A hallmark of neurogenic hypertension is the exacerbation of respiratory-modulated SNA (RespSNA) and resulting blood pressure Traube-Hering (TH) waves, which emerges during the prehypertensive period and contributes to disease development. Carotid bodies (CBs), the peripheral chemoreceptors involved in the hypoxic response, are hyperactive in hypertensive patients and animal models. Their chronic intermittent stimulation, as seen in obstructive sleep apnoea, promotes hypertension characterised by exacerbated RespSNA and TH waves. Yet, their causal role in initiating these changes remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether acute intermittent CB stimulations could directly enhance RespSNA, TH waves and blood pressure from a physiological baseline, using the in situ working heart-brainstem preparation in rats. Four brief CB stimulations with sodium cyanide, mimicking acute intermittent hypoxia, were sufficient to induce a prolonged (>20 min) increase in both inspiratory and late expiratory RespSNA bursts, TH waves and perfusion pressure, with these effects being prevented by carotid sinus denervation. These changes were accompanied by a reconfiguration of central respiratory and cardiovascular control, including elevated respiratory heart rate variability and enhanced respiratory drive targeting upper airway and abdominal muscles. Our findings demonstrate that acute intermittent CB activation triggers sustained RespSNA and elevation of TH waves, supporting its potential role in development of hypertension. Our data also suggest that CBs play a key role in initiating this respiratory-cardiovascular plasticity and that central mechanisms might contribute to its long-term maintenance. KEY POINTS: Carotid body (CB) overactivity is implicated in sympathetic excitation and development of hypertension, but its direct role in initiating respiratory-cardiovascular dysfunction remains unresolved. We tested whether brief, repeated CB stimulations could trigger lasting changes in breathing and blood pressure control from a physiological baseline. In rats, only four stimulations induced a persistent increase in respiratory-modulated sympathetic activity, elevating blood pressure fluctuations (Traube-Hering waves) and mean blood pressure. These effects, prevented by carotid sinus denervation, were linked to enhanced respiratory-cardiovascular coupling and altered upper airway and abdominal motor control. Our findings reveal that short-term CB activation can induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling, relevant to both physiological adaptations and hypertension pathogenesis.

papers.title: [Post-traumatic growth in male erectile dysfunction patients: The role of family function, fear of disease progression and self-perceived burden].
papers.abstract: Objective The aim of this study is to investigate the current status of post-traumatic growth (PTG) in male erectile dysfunction （ED） patients, and to analyze the mediating effects of self-perceived burden and family functioning on the fear of disease progression's chain-mediated impact on PTG. Methods A total of 386 male ED patients admitted to the Second Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University between June 2023 and December 2024 were selected as research subjects. The study employed questionnaires including the General Information Questionnaire, International Erectile Dysfunction Index (IIEF), Family Caregiving Index (APGAR), Post-Traumatic Growth Index (PTGI), Simplified Fear of Disease Progression Scale (FoP-Q-SF) and Self-Perceived Burden Scale (SPBS). Pearson correlation analysis was used to assess relationships among PTG, self-perceived burden, family functioning and fear of disease progression. While structural equation modeling (SEM) was conducted using Amos 21.0 software to evaluate mediating effects. Results Among 386 male ED patients, the Patient-Reported Global Score (PTG) scored （51.37±7.24）, family function （8.21±1.12）, fear of disease progression （35.28±5.31）, and self-perceived burden （32.56±5.26）. Age, shame, chronic diseases, cultural factors, social stress and sleep quality were statistically significant predictors for PTG (P<0.05). PTG showed positive correlations with family function and fear of disease progression, but negative correlations with self-perceived burden (all P<0.05). Family function exhibited significant negative correlations with both fear of disease progression and self-perceived burden (P<0.01). Fear of disease progression and self-reported burden demonstrated positive correlations (P<0.05). The study confirmed a chain mediation effect of family function on PTG, with the total indirect effect accounting for 34.23% of the total effect. Specifically, the specific mediation effect of fear of disease progression accounted for 16.99%, self-perceived burden for 14.25%, and the combined chain mediation effect for 2.99%. Conclusion The chain mediation effect between fear of disease progression, self-perceived burden, family function and PTG was established in male erectile dysfunction patients. This confirms that family function can influence PTG by moderating the levels of fear of disease progression and self-perceived burden.
papers.journal: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology
keywords: erectile dysfunction; post-traumatic growth; family functioning; fear of disease progression; self-perceived burden

papers.title: Invasive Monitoring in Acute Liver Failure.
papers.abstract: Acute liver failure (ALF) is a rapidly progressive condition marked by severe hepatic dysfunction, coagulopathy, and high short-term mortality driven largely by cerebral edema and circulatory collapse. Because neurological deterioration and hemodynamic instability can evolve unpredictably and interact dynamically, continuous physiologic monitoring is central to management. Invasive intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring provides the most direct assessment of intracranial dynamics and supports cerebral perfusion pressure-oriented therapy; however, its routine use remains controversial due to limited outcome data and substantial hemorrhagic risk in the setting of severe coagulopathy. Current evidence, largely observational, favors a selective approach to ICP monitoring in patients with advanced encephalopathy or rapidly worsening neurological status, particularly in experienced centers. Noninvasive adjuncts, including optic nerve sheath ultrasound, transcranial Doppler, and electroencephalography, offer complementary information but do not replace direct ICP measurement. Hemodynamic monitoring, anchored by continuous arterial pressure measurement and central venous access, is indispensable for maintaining systemic perfusion and protecting cerebral blood flow. Advanced cardiac output monitoring and echocardiography further enable individualized fluid and vasopressor strategies. Overall, a multimodal, physiology-driven monitoring framework that integrates neurological and circulatory assessment is essential to optimize outcomes in ALF.

papers.title: Exploring the role of nicotine and smoking in sleep behaviours: A multi-variable Mendelian randomisation study.
papers.abstract: Increased nicotine exposure (resulting from greater cigarette consumption and/or slower nicotine metabolism) may directly affect sleep and could underlie relationships between smoking and sleep behaviours identified previously. We conducted a Mendelian randomisation (MR) study to explore whether nicotine metabolism has a causal effect on sleep behaviours. Our main analysis method was inverse-variance weighted (IVW) Multivariable MR, which was used to examine the independent effects of nicotine metabolism and smoking heaviness on sleep behaviours. The model was developed to provide insights into the potential role of nicotine exposure. The genome-wide association summary data for these analyses were sourced from published genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary-level data, or GWAS conducted within the UK Biobank. Primary analyses focused on current smokers of European descent (N = 5185 to 487 153). We used genetic proxies of the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR), cigarettes per day (CPD), and sleep behaviours (chronotype [being an "evening" person versus a "morning" person], ease of getting up in the morning, insomnia symptoms, napping, daytime sleepiness and sleep duration). Higher NMR (consistent with lower circulating nicotine levels per cigarette smoked) decreased the likelihood of being an "evening" person when accounting for CPD in current smokers [beta coefficient (β) = -0.04, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.06 to -0.02, p < 0.001]. A higher NMR also increased the ease of getting up (β = 0.02, 95%CI 0.01 to 0.04, p = 0.001) and likelihood of napping (β = 0.02, 95%CI 0.01 to 0.03, p < 0.001) in current smokers. There was no consistent evidence for effects of NMR or CPD on insomnia symptoms or sleep duration, although increased sleep duration lowered NMR among current smokers (β = -0.43, 95%CI -0.74 to -0.12, p = 0.007), without corresponding effects on smoking heaviness. Among current smokers, nicotine metabolism may play a direct role in the relationship between smoking and certain sleep behaviours, particularly those related to circadian preference and daytime alertness, independent of smoking heaviness. There is some evidence that sleep duration may influence nicotine metabolism.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
papers.abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation's largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health.
