authors: Sleep Disorders Rehabilitation Professional Committee of Chinese Association of Rehabilitation Medicine
Community and Primary Care Working Committee of Chinese Sleep Research Society

papers.title: [Clinical implementation pathway and standardized measures for the "five prescriptions" in the treatment of adult obesity in China].
papers.abstract: The prevalence of overweight and obesity continues to increase globally. Obesity is a chronic, relapsing disease and a major risk factor for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and several malignancies. Drawing on current guidelines, expert consensus statements, systematic reviews, and pivotal randomized trials, this article proposes an integrated framework of five prescriptions for Chinese adults with obesity: nutrition, exercise, mental health and behavioral care, smoking cessation and alcohol restriction, and pharmacotherapy. Implementation begins with comprehensive assessment and risk stratification. Nutrition and exercise form the foundation, while mental health and behavioral support connect the interventions, sleep is managed through a stratified pathway. Smoking cessation and alcohol restriction support long-term risk reduction, and pharmacotherapy provides evidence-based intensification for eligible patients. This framework translates complex, long-term, relapse-prone obesity care into a standardized pathway that is assessable, prescribable, actionable, monitorable, iterative, and sustainable.

papers.title: Assessing variation in inpatient sleep opportunity and associated patient-reported sleep quality: An academic hospital-based observational study.
papers.abstract: Overnight interruptions are common in a hospital setting, but the impact of these interruptions on the opportunity for sleep in the general inpatient population and association with perceived sleep quality is unknown. To measure inpatient overnight sleep interruptions, their variation across adult hospital units, and associations between sleep opportunity and patient-reported sleep quality. Retrospective observational study using electronic health record data for an academic medical center in the Midwest United States. The cohort consisted of adult patient hospital admissions between September 2023 and August 2025, limited to nights on general acute medical and surgical units. Overnight interruptions from medication administration, vital checks, or lab collection were organized into 20-min interruptive episodes. Corresponding longest and total uninterrupted sleep opportunities and patient-reported sleep quality were assessed. Among 46,916 patient admissions, the longest uninterrupted sleep opportunity (LUSO) per patient-night averaged 3 h 40 min, and total uninterrupted sleep opportunity (TUSO) averaged approximately 6 h 30 min. Sleep opportunity variation was seen across individual hospital units, and even more across multiple admissions per patient. Both LUSO and TUSO were positively associated with level of patient-reported sleep quality. Inpatient sleep opportunities vary by admission and hospital unit, averaging under 4 h for the longest uninterrupted sleep opportunity on a given night. Sleep opportunity duration is associated with perceived sleep quality and could be used to assess sleep quality improvement interventions.

papers.title: Symptom-Level Comorbidity Patterns Between Depression and Internet Gaming Disorder Among Adolescents: Evidence from Longitudinal Network Analysis with Gender Considerations.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a period with an increased risk for the co-occurrence of depression and Internet gaming disorder (IGD), yet we still know little about how specific symptoms of these two conditions influence each other over time. In this study, we applied cross-lagged panel network analysis to two-wave data from a community sample of 538 adolescents (Mean age = 12.51 years; 53.7 percent female). Potential gender differences in the network structure were examined. In the overall sample and in both gender groups, depressive symptoms consistently predicted later gaming-related problems, whereas no reverse cross-disorder pathways were retained. In particular, suicidal ideation and psychomotor symptoms emerged as bridge symptoms linking depression and IGD, while sleep problems showed moderate outgoing expected influence in the overall symptom network. While boys and girls showed broadly similar patterns, some differences emerged in how specific symptoms were connected and which symptoms were most influential. These findings clarify the longitudinal symptom-level associations between depression and IGD in adolescents, suggesting that addressing key depressive symptoms may help reduce the risk of later IGD.

papers.title: A Portrait of Anxiety and Depression in Parkinson's Disease: Prevalence, Clinical Correlates, and Treatment Gaps.
papers.abstract: Non-motor symptoms (NMS), specifically anxiety and depression are major drivers of disability in Parkinson's disease (PD). Prevalence estimates remain inconsistent because of differences in population samples, diagnostic criteria, and symptom overlap, contributing to underdiagnosis and undertreatment. This retrospective, cross-sectional study examined the prevalence, comorbidity, and clinical correlates of anxiety and depression using dimensional severity scales and multivariate modeling. We retrospectively analyzed de-identified records from 1221 patients assessed by a single neurologist specializing in PD patient care. Mood symptom severity was evaluated using Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) and Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) criteria. Logistic regression models identified associated factors for relevant anxiety (BAI ≥13) and depression (BDI ≥14). Clinically relevant anxiety (42%) and depression (30%) and anxiety-depression comorbidity (24%) were found to be consistent with previous estimates, with a high prevalence of mild depression (33%). Regression models identified sleep disturbance as a primary associated factor for both mood symptoms. Functional impairments involving hygiene, walking, swallowing, sensory complaints, and speech were associated with one or both mood symptoms. Left lower-extremity bradykinesia and right-sided tremor were associated with both mood symptoms. Significant "treatment" and "remission" gaps were also observed, as prescriptions for anxiolytics and antidepressants were significantly associated with relevant anxiety and depression. These findings highlight pervasive diagnostic and therapeutic gaps and the relationship between mood symptoms and functional disability. The limited efficacy of pharmacological monotherapy underscores the need for multi-dimensional tools and integrated treatment approaches to improve recognition and management of mood symptoms in PD.

papers.title: Aluminum Foil Substrates Support Solvent-Free Raman Analysis of Skin Lipids.
papers.abstract: Sebum, a lipid-rich biofluid secreted onto the skin surface, holds promise as a non-invasive biomarker source but poses analytical challenges due to its hydrophobicity. Here, we demonstrate that aluminum foil substrates enable direct, solvent-free sampling and Raman spectroscopic analysis of human sebum, preserving key vibrational signatures of lipids, proteins, and carotenoids. We compared unprocessed sebum with chloroform/methanol and diethyl ether extraction methods in three volunteers, finding that solvent-free sampling yields more intense and chemically rich Raman spectra, while solvent-based methods attenuate signals and introduce compositional bias. Differential spectral analysis revealed that solvent extraction modifies the carbonyl and hydrocarbon stretching regions in a solvent-dependent manner. Our technical note focuses specifically on how sample processing affects the Raman spectral signature of sebum, underscoring the importance of solvent-free approaches and providing a methodological baseline for standardized Raman-based sebum analysis.

papers.title: Sleep Patterns, Sleep Hygiene, and Behavioral Problems in Primary School Children: A Cross-Sectional Study in İzmir, Turkey.
papers.abstract: This retrospective observational study aimed to evaluate the regulatory effects of sensory integration (SI)- based interventions on sensory processing patterns in children aged 7 to 36 months without diagnosed developmental disorders. The intervention group (n = 30) received individualized sensory integration support for at least 6 weeks, while the control group (n = 30) did not receive any specialized support. All participants were assessed using the Sensory Profile (7-36 months). The intervention group showed significantly higher mean scores across all 4 sensory processing quadrants-Low Registration, Sensation Seeking, Sensory Sensitivity, and Sensation Avoiding-compared to the control group (P < .001). These results suggest that early SI support enhances environmental awareness, behavioral regulation, and modulation of sensory thresholds, even in asymptomatic children. Sensory integration interventions may provide protective and regulatory benefits beyond clinical indications. Findings support the inclusion of sensory screening in early developmental monitoring and the integration of preventive SI strategies in pediatric care models.

papers.title: Multimodal synthesis of neural correlates of motor imagery after spinal cord injury: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) profoundly disrupts motor output while also reshaping central motor systems. Motor imagery (MI) provides a valuable window into retained motor-related neural processes because it enables investigation of covert motor state generation in the absence of overt movement. However, evidence on MI after SCI remains fragmented across neurophysiological and neuroimaging modalities. The objective of this review was to systematically synthesize evidence on the neural correlates of MI after SCI across electroencephalography (EEG), functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), magnetoencephalography (MEG), and intracortical recordings. A systematic search of MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, and EBSCOhost was conducted from database inception to March 2026. Original studies were included if they involved individuals with SCI, used an explicit MI task, and reported MI-related neural outcomes derived from EEG, fMRI, MEG, or intracortical recordings. Because of substantial heterogeneity in injury profiles, task paradigms, modalities, and neural outcome measures, a narrative synthesis was performed. Thirty-four studies met the inclusion criteria, including 15 EEG, 10 fMRI, 4 MEG, and 5 intracortical recording studies. Across modalities, MI-related neural activity remained detectable after SCI, with evidence spanning oscillatory responses, regional recruitment, network organization, and fine-grained neural representations. Many studies also described altered recruitment patterns, modified connectivity, atypical task-related modulation, or changes in representational structure. Findings varied according to injury phenotype, chronicity, task design, and analytical framework. The four modalities provided complementary evidence on post-SCI motor imagery across temporal, spatial, network, and neuronal scales. Available evidence indicates that MI-related neural activity is generally detectable after SCI, although its organization is often altered. A multimodal perspective is therefore necessary for understanding both the persistence and the reshaping of motor representations after injury. These findings support continued investigation of MI in neurorehabilitation and neurotechnology, while also highlighting the need for approaches that account for post-injury heterogeneity.

papers.title: Machine learning framework to enhance and automate cardiovascular outpatient triage for patients with atrial fibrillation.
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent arrhythmia, placing a substantial burden on the healthcare system. Patients with AF are cared for in a variety of settings, including primary care and cardiovascular (CV) clinics, while some require cardiac electrophysiology (EP) clinics that offer specialized drugs or procedures. Triage of AF referrals to these specific clinics will lead to timely and proper care and reduce inefficiency in the health system. The goal is to develop a machine learning framework to triage the likelihood of patient referrals to EP-directed treatments. We retrospectively analyzed 6,755 patients who were referred to CV with a referral diagnosis of AF. Data encompassed patient demographics, relevant comorbidities, medications, prior procedures, medical notes analyzed using natural language processing (NLP), and Holter monitoring data. A two-stage framework, predicting the necessity for specialized EP care, was developed: the construction of the machine learning model, followed by post-refinement based on established clinical criteria. The Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) model emerged as the most effective model in the first stage, achieving an area under the curve of 0.77, an accuracy of 72%, a true positive rate (TPR) of 67%, and a false positive rate of 23%. The post-refinement stage further improved TPR to as much as 83%. This framework resulted in increased identification of EP-direct patient care from the current reported 20% to 46%. Our framework effectively identifies patients who are likely to require specialized EP care, thereby enhancing the automation of the AF referral triage process and potentially improving efficiency.
papers.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making

papers.title: Circadian rhythm dysregulation and brain functional connectivity alterations in stroke patients: an exploratory study of peripheral and central clock interactions.
papers.abstract: The human circadian rhythm system is governed by a transcriptional-translational feedback loop of clock genes, including Bmal1, which exhibits a near-24-hour oscillatory period. Emerging evidence highlights the critical contribution of circadian genes to stroke pathogenesis and outcomes, yet mechanistic insights into their regulatory roles remain limited. To bridge this knowledge gap, we aimed to determine whether the serum of stroke patients could affect changes in the molecular clock and whether such changes in the molecular clock were potentially linked to abnormal brain functional connectivity in stroke patients. This prospective case-control study included 17 patients with stroke and 17 age-matched healthy participants. All participants were required to complete a standardized comprehensive questionnaire. Transfected human osteosarcoma cells (U2OS) stably expressing Bmal1-dluc reporters were treated with serum from both groups to monitor changes in the daily oscillation period of Bmal1. We also compared the changes in resting-state hypothalamic intrinsic functional connectivity(FC) between the two groups. Further, we explored the correlation between the differences in FC between the two groups and the daily oscillation period of Bmal1. Compared to the healthy control group, stroke patients exhibited a significantly prolonged peripheral Bmal1 circadian oscillation period (24.32 ± 0.41 h vs. 23.81 ± 0.48 h, t = 3.352, p = 0.002). In FC analysis, the stroke group showed enhanced connectivity from the hypothalamus to the right occipital lobe and the right insular region. Notably, the degree of this connectivity enhancement demonstrated a significant positive correlation with the length of Bmal1 oscillation period (r = 0.369, p = 0.032; r = 0.393, p = 0.022). Our findings suggest that serum from stroke patients lengthens the circadian period in U2OS cells and may be associated with alterations in brain functional connectivity. However, the small sample size limits statistical power, and these exploratory results require replication in larger independent cohorts. ChiCTR2000031671(April 4, 2020).

papers.title: Psychological distress among acute coronary syndrome patients - a descriptive cross-sectional study in patients managed at an interventional cardiology unit in Sri Lanka.
papers.abstract: Mental health issues are a globally prevalent problem. Psychological distress (PD) is an emotional and behavioural response to a stressor and can even lead to mental health disease. It is also associated with cardiovascular disease including acute coronary syndrome. A cross-sectional study was conducted to assess psychological distress using a Kessler's psychological distress scale (K10) in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome in a primary percutaneous coronary intervention centre in Sri Lanka. Hundred and fifty-seven patients were enrolled. Data was collected from an interviewer-and self-administered questionnaires. Patient demographics, socio-economic, behavioural and clinical & therapeutic details were obtained and analysed using Chi-square tests and Polytomous Universal Model (PLUM) ordinal regression for cross comparison with varying levels of psychological distress [no distress, mild distress, moderate distress or severe distress]. The mean age was 52.9 ± 11.01 years and 40.8% of the sampled patients had varying levels of psychological distress. On initial bivariate analysis screening recent emotional distress, inadequate sleep, regular religious activity showed statistically significant correlation with PD (P < 0.05). However, when adjusting for confounders in the multivariate PLUM ordinal regression only recent emotional disturbance (P < 0.001) [aOR = 19.71, 95% CI:8.00-48.52) and inadequate sleep duration (P = 0.019) [aOR = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.17-5.62] retained independent significance as predictors of distress severity. Other behavioural and clinical disease attributes became attenuated in the multivariate model. Psychological distress is prevalent among patients with acute coronary syndrome. The immediate emotional burden after ACS is independently associated with patients' pre-existing emotional baseline and lifestyle biology rather than clinical disease and its severity.

papers.title: Distribution of device-measured 24-hour movement behaviours across the cognitive spectrum in older adults: the HUNT study.
papers.abstract: Key daily physical activities (e.g., standing and walking), postures (sitting and lying), and sleep constitute the 24-h day and have distinct health effects and functional implications. Traditionally studied separately, the distribution of these movement behaviours and sleep across the cognitive spectrum remains insufficiently characterised. We aimed to describe and compare the distribution of 24-h movement behaviours and sleep across the cognitive spectrum. We analysed cross-sectional, population-based data from 4,699 community-dwelling older adults (≥ 70 years) participating in the HUNT4 70 + study. Cognitive status was classified as mild cognitive impairment (MCI, n = 1,690) or dementia (n = 360) according to DSM-5 criteria. Participants not classified with MCI or dementia were categorised as cognitively unimpaired. Accelerometers worn on the thigh and lower back (≤ 7 days) were used to assess standing, walking, sitting, lying awake, and sleep using validated machine-learning models. Inverse probability weighting and multiple imputation by chained equations were used to address selection bias. Group differences were examined using survey-weighted regression models adjusted for potential confounders including age, sex, education, marital status, self-rated health, obesity, depression, alcohol consumption, and smoking. In fully adjusted models, older adults with MCI spent less time sitting (ß -12.4 [95% CI -20.0, -4.4] min/ 24 h) and more time lying awake (ß 10.3 [95% CI 2.7, 17.9]) and sleeping (ß 3.9 [95% CI 0.8, 7.0] min/24 h) than their cognitively unimpaired peers (all p < 0.05), while time spent standing and walking was similar between the two groups. In fully adjusted models, older adults with dementia spent less time standing (ß -29.0 [95% CI -41.3, -16.5] and ß -30.3 [95% CI -42.5, -18.2] min/24 h) and walking (ß -16.1 [95% CI -19.9, -12.4] and ß -17.2 [95% CI -20.9, -13.4] min/24 h), and more time lying awake (ß 36.3 [95% CI 17.1, 55.4] and ß 46.5 [95% CI 28.7, 64.5] min/24 h), than those with MCI and cognitively unimpaired peers (all p ≤ 0.001), and more time sleeping (ß 7.5 [95% CI 0.9, 14.9] min/24 h) than their cognitively unimpaired peers (p = 0.04). Across the cognitive spectrum, older adults exhibit distinct distributions of 24-h movement behaviours and sleep. The clinical importance of the observed differences remains unknown, and future research on the independent and compositional effects of these behaviours is warranted.
papers.journal: European review of aging and physical activity : official journal of the European Group for Research into Elderly and Physical Activity

papers.title: Perioperative esketamine and postoperative sleep quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
papers.abstract: Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is common among surgical patients and adversely affects recovery. The benefits of perioperative esketamine on sleep remain incompletely defined. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ketamine or esketamine with saline or other drugs for postoperative sleep quality were identified through a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library until 6 September 2025. The primary outcome was postoperative sleep quality scores, and effect sizes were calculated using the ratio of means (ROM). Secondary outcomes included incidence of PSD, postoperative pain and depression scores, and adverse events. Twenty-three trials including 2868 participants met inclusion criteria. Esketamine improved sleep quality on postoperative day (POD) 1 (ROM, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.80 to 0.90; P < 0.001; I2 = 84%; 21 studies), POD 2 (ROM, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.57 to 0.93; P = 0.01; I2 = 92%; 8 studies), POD 3 (ROM, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.90 to 0.99; P = 0.02; I2 = 25%; 12 studies), and POD 7 (ROM, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.82 to 0.95; P = 0.001; I2 = 36%; 8 studies); no benefit was observed at 1 month. The incidence of PSD was reduced on PODs 1 through 3 (RRs, 0.71, 0.70, and 0.61, respectively; all P ≤ 0.01), with no effect on POD 7. Esketamine also lowered postoperative pain and depression scores. However, it increased drowsiness (RR, 12.64; 95% CI, 6.04 to 26.46; P < 0.001; I2 = 21%). Perioperative esketamine is associated with short-term improvements in postoperative sleep quality and a lower incidence of PSD, alongside reductions in pain and depressive symptoms. However, these benefits are accompanied by an increased risk of drowsiness, and the current evidence does not yet support routine clinical use. Larger multinational trials are warranted.

papers.title: Effect of orofacial myofunctional therapy with auto-monitoring on the apnea-hypopnea index in patients with mild-to-moderate obstructive sleep apnea: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is a promising treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but protocols vary and outcomes are inconsistent. The primary aim was to evaluate the effect of a standardized OMT protocol on changes in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). Secondary aims were to analyze associations between OMT adherence and change in objective and self-reported outcomes. Treatment-naive adults with mild-to-moderate OSA were randomized in a multicenter trial to 12 weeks of OMT or a waitlist control group. Three nights of polysomnography were completed before and after the intervention. Adherence was registered electronically. The primary outcome was change in AHI. Pre-defined secondary outcomes were changes in desaturation measures and in the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score. Intention-to-treat analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models, whereas per-protocol analyses were based on analysis of covariance. A total of 104 participants (mean age 47.1 ± 12.2 years) were included. Intention-to-treat analysis included 104 participants (52 treatment, 52 waitlist) and showed no significant effect of OMT on AHI. Difference in AHI change between groups was 0.6 (95% CI -3.3 to 4.5; P = .774). Overall mean adherence across all days and participants was 64.6% (95% CI 61.0 to 76.8). Higher adherence was not associated with significantly greater reduction in AHI (β = -0.1, 95% CI -0.2 to 0.1; P = .353). No change was detected in pre-defined secondary outcomes. Twelve weeks of standardized OMT had no significant effect on AHI, desaturation measures or ESS score in treatment-naive patients newly diagnosed with OSA. Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is increasingly considered a non-invasive treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but existing evidence is heterogeneous and often limited by methodological shortcomings. We therefore conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of a standardized OMT protocol in adults newly diagnosed with mild-to-moderate OSA. The intervention did not improve pre-defined OSA outcomes, highlighting the importance of rigorous trials even when results are negative. These findings help refine the evidence base for OMT in adults with OSA while supporting continued investigation of alternative protocols and populations stratified by endo- or phenotyping. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT06079073, URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06079073 , First submission: 2023-08-23.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine

papers.title: Different Pipelines, Different EEG Microstate Results: Evidence from Dementia Samples.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) microstate analysis has been proposed as a potential biomarker for neurological disorders, yet the influence of analytic pipeline choices on clinical findings remains unclear. Resting-state EEG from patients with Alzheimer's disease (n = 36), frontotemporal dementia (n = 23), and healthy controls (n = 29) was analyzed using multiple microstate pipelines combining k-means or atomize-agglomerate hierarchical clustering with different temporal-smoothing conditions. Bayesian ANCOVA showed that evidence for group differences varied substantially across pipelines, particularly as a function of temporal smoothing. Rank-correlation analyses further demonstrated reduced agreement between smoothed and unsmoothed pipelines, indicating that smoothing altered the relative ordering of microstate temporal parameters across participants. To assess methodological stability, intra-subject split-half analyses were performed. Microstate topographies showed > 92% shared variance between independent data halves, whereas the reliability of duration, occurrence, and coverage varied across pipelines. Unsmoothed pipelines generally showed equal or greater split-half reliability for selected microstate B measures, and the reproducibility of clinical effect sizes differed by clustering algorithm and diagnostic contrast. These findings demonstrate that temporal smoothing and clustering choices can substantially influence the reliability and clinical interpretation of EEG microstate measures, underscoring the need for explicit pipeline validation in biomarker studies.

papers.title: Negative consequences of sleep disturbance in individuals with limb loss.
papers.abstract: To identify the association between sleep disturbance with physical function and psychological outcomes in individuals with limb loss. This cross-sectional study included 218 community ambulating individuals with at least one amputation, recruited from Military treatment facilities, community events, and prosthetic clinics. Participants' demographics were obtained from self-reported questionnaires. The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS)-29 scores were used to assess sleep disturbance, physical function, anxiety, depression, fatigue, pain interference, and social participation. Sleep disturbance data were used to categorize the participants into three mutually exclusive groups: no sleep disturbance, mild sleep disturbance, and moderate to severe sleep disturbance. One-way analyses of variance (ANOVA) were used to determine if differences existed in PROMIS scores between the three sleep disturbance categories. Results showed that as compared to individuals with no sleep disturbance, those with moderate to severe sleep disturbance had worse physical function; higher levels of anxiety, depression, fatigue, and pain interference, and less social participation. In addition, a difference was noted between the mild and the moderate to severe groups indicating worse depression, fatigue, social participation, and pain interference. When compared to the no sleep disturbance group, the mild disturbance group demonstrated worse physical function and fatigue (all P < 0.05). Results reflect that higher levels of sleep disturbance are associated with worse functional and psychological outcome measures in individuals with limb loss. Findings from this study also indicate that a higher threshold of sleep disturbance is required to impact levels of depression, social participation, and pain interference.

papers.title: Prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with intracranial aneurysms.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with various cardiovascular and cerebrovascular conditions; however, its prevalence among patients with intracranial aneurysms (IAs) remains insufficiently characterized. Emerging evidence suggests that OSA may contribute to IA formation, progression, and outcomes after rupture. This study included 244 participants: 84 IA patients without prior clinical suspicion of OSA and 160 OSA-symptomatic comparators. Overnight respiratory polygraphy (RP) was used to assess apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and presence of OSA. Group differences were analyzed using models adjusted for age, BMI, and sex. Among IA patients, 50.0% had findings consistent with OSA on RP (AHI ≥ 5 events per hour), of whom 27.4% were classified as mild, 15.5% as moderate, and 7.1% as severe. The corresponding proportions in the OSA-symptomatic comparison group were 71.3% for overall OSA, and 36.3%, 18.1%, and 16.9%, for mild, moderate, and severe, respectively. Log-transformed AHI in IA patients did not differ significantly from that in the symptomatic comparison group (F(1,238) = 1.88, p = 0.171, partial η2 = 0.008). RP findings demonstrated a high and largely unrecognized burden of OSA in IA patients. These findings support more systematic and proactive screening for OSA in IA patients, particularly among those with established OSA risk factors.

papers.title: EEG functional connectivity as a prognostic biomarker of adaptive function in autistic people.
papers.abstract: Many autistic people have challenges with adaptive function, impacting education, employment and independent-living goals. Adaptive function outcomes of autistic people vary considerably, which makes planning for future needs challenging. Here, using a developmentally sensitive approach, we investigated if cortico-cortical functional connectivity - a core neurobiological feature that differs in autism - could predict longitudinal changes in adaptive function in autistic people. Using electroencephalography in 150 autistic and 159 non-autistic participants aged 6-31 years, we investigated if mean degree and network organisation (small-world index) predict longitudinal changes in adaptive function over 19-months. We found that small-world index significantly predicted changes in adaptive function in autistic people across the entire age-range. Predictive performance was best for autistic youth (15-24-year-olds), where mean degree and small-world index explained 21 and 30% of additional variance in outcomes, respectively, outperforming measures of intelligence and autistic features. In categorising binary (improved versus not-improved) outcomes, the model containing mean degree had an AUC of 0.84 [95% CI: 0.71-0.97] in 15-24-year-olds, while that containing small-world index had an AUC of 0.76 [95% CI: 0.63-0.89] across the 6-31-year age-range. Both metrics demonstrated properties desired in prognostic biomarkers: high test-retest reliability and convergence with underlying biology (significant associations with genetic variation in brain volume-related genes). Thus, we demonstrate the first evidence that electroencephalography-derived functional connectivity metrics show promise as prognostic biomarkers of adaptive function in autistic people. Potential precision-medicine applications include stratifying participants in clinical trials and identifying those at risk of declining function in clinical settings.

papers.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes.
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode-skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

papers.title: Alcohol and Opioids Modulate Excitatory Inputs to the SCN.
papers.abstract: Disturbance of circadian rhythms is a hallmark of substance use disorders, with depressant drugs often causing soporific effects such as reduced sleep latency. The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the hypothalamus is the central circadian pacemaker in mammals, regulating daily rhythms in physiology and behavior. However, the cellular mechanisms through which depressants alter SCN function remain poorly defined. We used whole-cell patch clamp electrophysiology in coronal brain slices to examine how alcohol and opioids modulate excitatory glutamatergic transmission onto SCN neurons. Ethanol effects were examined acutely and following chronic exposure paradigms. Optogenetic stimulation was used to activate either retinohypothalamic tract (RHT) input or μ-opioid receptor-expressing (MOR+) terminals, and MOR agonists were used to assess opioid-mediated effects on synaptic transmission. We show that acute application of ethanol enhances SCN firing rates during the inactive locomotor stage of circadian rhythms (daytime for rodents). In contrast, chronic alcohol exposure reduces glutamatergic drive. We also found that activating MOR+ terminals via an excitatory channelrhodopsin transgenically expressed in MOR+ neurons produced bidirectional modulation of SCN firing and that MOR+ inputs formed functional glutamatergic synapses onto SCN neurons. We also found that chronic alcohol consumption significantly altered MOR-dependent modulation of SCN neuronal activity, demonstrating an interaction between ethanol exposure and opioidergic signaling. Notably, MOR-mediated transmission could be suppressed by the MOR agonists DAMGO and fentanyl. Together, these findings reveal that both alcohol and opioids modulate glutamatergic input to the SCN. This work establishes the SCN as a novel target of depressant substances and highlights glutamatergic transmission as a key point of vulnerability in circadian dysregulation associated with substance use.

papers.title: Functional brain signatures of successful cognitive aging.
papers.abstract: Cognitive aging trajectories vary markedly. While many older adults experience gradual decline in memory and executive function, some maintain high cognitive performance well into advanced age. Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying this variability carries important implications for early detection of unfavorable aging trajectories and the development of interventions. Here, we review functional brain signatures associated with successful cognitive aging in humans, integrating evidence from functional magnetic resonance imaging and electroencephalography within a unified conceptual framework of brain maintenance and compensation. Across both modalities, evidence increasingly links successful cognitive aging to the preservation of youth-like neural dynamics, while the contribution of compensatory neural recruitment remains empirically contested and methodologically difficult to establish.

papers.title: Sex differences in weight loss and metabolic outcomes following bariatric surgery: the Dutch bariatric quality registry.
papers.abstract: Sex-specific differences in body fat distribution and cardiometabolic health may contribute to distinct outcomes following metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). To investigate sex-specific differences in weight loss and cardiometabolic outcomes following MBS. Nationwide bariatric quality registry, the Netherlands. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Dutch Audit for Treatment of Obesity. A total of 14,190 adult patients who underwent primary Roux-en-Y gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy between 2014 and 2018 were included. Primary outcomes were percentage of total weight loss (%TWL) and changes in hypertension, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea syndrome. Recurrent weight gain was defined as regaining more than 30% of the weight lost since surgery at 5-year follow-up. At baseline, men had a significantly higher prevalence of obesity-related co-morbidities than women. Women achieved greater relative weight loss at both 1 year (33.2% versus 30.4%, P < .001) and 5 years (28.9% versus 25.9%, P < .001). Men showed higher observed resolution rates for cardiometabolic complications, including hypertension (34.6% versus 23.7%) and type 2 diabetes (27.7% versus 13.6%; both P < .01). Recurrent weight gain at 5 years was 9.9% in men and 10.9% in women (P < .001). No statistically significant difference in %TWL between Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy was observed (P = .054). Women achieved 2.8 percentage points greater %TWL than men after 1 year and 3.0 percentage points greater %TWL after 5 years. Men had higher observed resolution rates of obesity-related co-morbidities, although these findings should be interpreted in the context of their higher baseline metabolic disease burden.
authors: Dutch Audit for Treatment of Obesity Research Group
papers.journal: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery

papers.title: Actigraphy-estimated rest-activity rhythm characteristics of adolescents by sociodemographic factors and their association with adiposity.
papers.abstract: Characterize 24-hour rest-activity rhythm patterns among adolescents transitioning from middle to high school and examine associations with adiposity outcomes. Longitudinal observational data from the Sleep and Growth Study were analyzed. Count per minute data from actigraphy were processed using ActCR and GGIR packages to estimate non-parametric and cosine-based rest-activity rhythm metrics. Sociodemographic factors (sex, race, grade level, parental education, household income), pubertal status, and season were captured. Adiposity outcomes (fat mass index and visceral fat area) were estimated using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Linear mixed-effects and quantile regression modeling were used to analyze the data. The analytical sample included 107 adolescents at baseline (45.8% female; mean [SD] age, 13.9 [0.4] years) and 85 adolescents at follow-up (50.6% female; mean [SD] age, 14.9 [0.4] years). In longitudinal mixed-effects models, adolescents in ninth grade, relative to eighth grade, exhibited lower mesor and amplitude, reduced day-to-day stability (lower interdaily stability), and greater within-day variability (higher intradaily variability). Irrespective of grade, female adolescents had higher amplitudes, advanced pubertal status associated with later timing of peak activity (later acrophase and M10 midpoint), and those from households with incomes ≥$100,000 had an earlier peak inactivity (earlier L5 midpoint). Rest-activity rhythm metrics were not associated with fat mass index, fat mass index z score, or visceral fat area in a pattern indicative of obesity using quantile regression. Rest-activity rhythm patterns changed from eighth to ninth grades, with select sociodemographic and developmental factors associated with rest-activity rhythm patterns. There was no evidence rest-activity rhythm patterns associated with clinically relevant levels of adiposity outcomes.

papers.title: Comb-Like EEG Pattern as an Early Diagnostic Clue in Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD): A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is a life-threatening inborn error of amino acid metabolism that often presents in the neonatal period with nonspecific symptoms such as poor feeding, lethargy, and seizures. Although newborn screening (NBS) enables early identification, false-negative results and delays in reporting may lead to missed or delayed diagnosis, resulting in severe neurologic injury. A characteristic EEG finding, the "comb-like rhythm," consisting of central- or frontocentral-predominant, sharply contoured 4-7 Hz theta bursts has been reported in MSUD. However, its diagnostic utility has not been systematically evaluated. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the comb-like rhythm as a diagnostic clue for MSUD. A systematic literature search was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines using MEDLINE and Embase databases up to May 18, 2026. Studies evaluating EEG findings in individuals with MSUD were included. Data on clinical presentation, biochemical findings, brain imaging, and EEG features were extracted and synthesized qualitatively. In addition, two neonatal cases from our institution were included. Associations of the comb-like EEG rhythm with patient age at EEG (neonatal vs. non-neonatal) and plasma leucine concentrations were evaluated using Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test. A total of 113 records were screened, and 18 studies were included, comprising 24 symptomatic cases including our two patients. Abnormal EEG findings were reported in 21 of 24 (88%). A comb-like pattern was exclusively observed in neonates with acute metabolic crisis (13/15 neonates [86.7%] vs. 0/9 non-neonates [0%], p < 0.0001). The comb-like rhythm was associated with higher plasma leucine concentrations (median, 3545 vs. 1782 μmol/L, p = 0.0033). The pattern often diminished or resolved following treatment or clinical stabilization. In our two patients, the comb-like rhythm contributed to raising diagnostic suspicion despite initially normal NBS results. The comb-like rhythm may serve as an adjunctive EEG marker that raises suspicion for acute MSUD, given its strong association with neonatal metabolic crisis and severe hyperleucinemia. Further studies are needed to clarify its pathophysiological basis and determine the clinical utility of EEG in MSUD crisis.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A

papers.title: The probability of self-related stimuli modulates heartbeat-evoked potentials.
papers.abstract: Interoception, the cortical processing of visceral signals, has been proposed as a foundation of self-processing. Heartbeat-evoked potentials (HEPs) provide a measure of interoceptive processing and have been linked to self-processing, but whether HEP modulations reflect self-specificity rather than familiarity and depend on probabilistic context remains unclear. We recorded EEG and ECG during passive listening to subject's own names (SON), familiar names (FN), and unfamiliar name (UN) under equal- and biased-probability conditions. In the equal-probability condition, HEP amplitudes were more positive for SON than for FN and UN over centro-parietal-occipital sites at 164-242 and 258-296 ms after the R peak, whereas FN and UN did not differ. This self-specific pattern was not detected under biased probabilities. Within-name comparisons revealed probability-related HEP effects for SON and UN with distinct spatiotemporal characteristics, indicating that stimulus probability did not produce a uniform effect across name types. The late positive potential showed a comparable probability-dependent self-specific pattern, and SON-evoked LPP amplitudes positively covaried with HEP amplitudes during SON perception across conditions. These findings indicate that self-specific HEP modulations depend on probabilistic context and is associated with relatively late external self-related processing, highlighting a context-sensitive relationship between interoceptive and external self-related processing.

papers.title: Multi-omics analyses of HFpEF progression and regression reveals multi-organ-specific metabolic dysregulation and impaired inflammation resolution.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex cardiometabolic syndrome with limited effective therapies. Given its heterogeneity, whether withdrawal of cardiometabolic stress reverses HFpEF-associated inflammatory, metabolic, and molecular remodeling remains unclear. To characterize multi-organ metabolic, molecular, and bioactive-lipid remodeling in an obesity-hypertension HFpEF model and determine the extent of recovery during an 8-week combined high-fat diet withdrawal and L-NAME cessation protocol using parallel multi-omics profiling. HFpEF was induced in C57BL/6 mice using a high-fat diet plus nitric oxide synthase inhibition(H + L). A regression cohort(R-H + L) underwent simultaneous return to standard chow and L-NAME cessation for 8 weeks. Multi-omics profiling included targeted and untargeted lipidomics, cardiac transcriptomics, metabolomics, fecal microbiome, and plasma short-chain fatty acid analyses, with detailed assessment of the left ventricle. H + L mice developed an obesity-hypertension HFpEF phenotype characterized by predominant diastolic dysfunction, concentric remodeling, hypertension, and increased fat mass. The combined regression of H + L protocol attenuated these phenotypic abnormalities but did not restore all measures to control levels. H + L was associated with multi-organ remodeling marked by altered arachidonic acid-derived oxylipid pathways, depletion of triacylglycerols and phospholipids, and enrichment of diacylglycerols and lysophospholipids, consistent with altered resolution-related lipid signaling. Cardiac transcriptomics revealed changes in immune, circadian, vascular, and mitochondrial gene programs, whereas metabolomics revealed altered energy, arginine, and redox metabolism. H + L was also associated with reduced microbial diversity and altered short-chain fatty acids, particularly acetate and propionate. Within the 8-week recovery window, partial reprogramming occurred, but differences remained in lipid signaling, metabolic stress responses, and microbiome-associated measures. The HFD/L-NAME model is accompanied by extensive multi-organ metabolic and molecular remodeling. Combined withdrawal of HFD/L-NAME attenuates the HFpEF phenotype however did not fully normalize molecular profiles within the 8-week recovery period. Persistent lipid-remodeling and metabolic dysregulation may represent potential therapeutic targets thus warrants pathway specific investigation.

papers.title: Beyond Movement Behaviours: Unravelling the Prospective Links Between 24-Hour Behavioural Composition and Affective Dynamics in Adolescent Athletes.
papers.abstract: While the full spectrum of 24-hour movement behaviours - encompassing sleep (SLP), sedentary behaviour (SB), light physical activity (LPA), structured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (S-MVPA), and unstructured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (US-MVPA) - is consistently linked to daily affective states in adolescent athletes, existing literature has rarely examined these behaviours as an interdependent time-use composition, and largely fails to disentangle the distinct effects of structured versus unstructured MVPA subdomains on emotional outcomes. Using a repeated-measures prospective daily design, this study included 161 adolescent athletes (101 males and 60 females). Accelerometers were used to quantify 24-h movement behaviours. Four affective dimensions were assessed through ecological momentary assessment (EMA): high-arousal positive affect, low-arousal positive affect, high-arousal negative affect, and low-arousal negative affect. Bayesian multilevel compositional models were used to estimate between- and within-person associations, while isotemporal substitution analyses evaluated the estimated effects of reallocating time between behaviours on next-day affect. Associations between 24-h behaviour compositions and next-day affect were more evident at the within-person level. A higher relative proportion of LPA was associated with higher high-arousal positive affect (0.305, 95% Bayesian credible interval [CrI] 0.255 to 0.354) and low-arousal positive affect (0.292, 95% CrI 0.245 to 0.338), and lower high-arousal negative affect (-0.231, 95% CrI -0.260 to -0.203) and low-arousal negative affect (-0.210, 95% CrI -0.236 to -0.185). In 30-min substitution analyses, reallocating time from other behaviours to LPA generally showed more favourable associations with next-day affect at both between- and within-person levels, although the associations varied across substitution pairs and affective dimensions. These findings highlight LPA as the behaviour most consistently associated with favourable next-day affect. Daily 24-h movement behaviour composition was prospectively associated with next-day affect in adolescent athletes. LPA showed the most consistent favourable associations with next-day affect, particularly when replacing SB. Promoting LPA may represent a feasible strategy for supporting affective wellbeing without adding to existing training demands.

papers.title: Breaking the Cycle: Barriers and Facilitators to Reducing Sedentary Behavior in Prostate Cancer Survivors-A Qualitative Study.
papers.abstract: Sedentary behavior is increasingly recognized as a distinct health concern among people living with and beyond cancer, yet little is known about how prostate cancer survivors understand and experience prolonged sitting in their everyday lives. To explore perceived barriers and facilitators that may hinder or support reducing Sedentary behavior among prostate cancer survivors. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 19 prostate cancer survivors recruited from a university research registry of prostate cancer survivors, community and cancer care organizations, and referrals. Eligibility were ≥18 years, diagnosed with localized or asymptomatic metastatic prostate cancer, not currently undergoing radiation or chemotherapy, being proficient in English, and having access to a webcam-enabled device. Interviews were conducted via Zoom between November 2024 and January 2025. Data was transcribed verbatim and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Three core themes emerged: 1) Making Sense of Sitting in Everyday Life; 2) Negotiating the Personal and Contextual Conditions for Sitting Less; 3) Sustaining Efforts to Sit Less. While participants were aware of the health risks of Sedentary behavior, many reported difficulties translating awareness into action. Key barriers included sleep disturbances, fatigue, aging concerns, chronic conditions (e.g., osteoporosis, plantar fasciitis), and treatment-related bodily changes. Social connections, routines, and personally meaningful motivations shaped how participants negotiated sedentary behavior in daily life. Findings underscore critical barriers (e.g., fatigue, comorbid conditions) and facilitators (e.g., social support) that should be prioritized in intervention design. Addressing these factors may improve the feasibility and effectiveness of sedentary behavior reduction strategies to enhance survivorship outcomes.

papers.title: Smoking, recent physical activity and diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions in lifetime bipolar-spectrum disorder: A nationally representative comparison with lifetime major depressive episode without bipolar disorder.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease contributes substantially to premature mortality in bipolar disorder, making modifiable health behaviours important clinical targets. We analyzed the 2022 Canadian Mental Health and Access to Care Survey, including 294 respondents with lifetime bipolar-spectrum disorder derived from the Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI; bipolar I, bipolar II, or algorithm-positive hypomania without bipolar I/II classification) and 938 with lifetime major depressive episode (MDE) without bipolar-spectrum disorder. Survey-weighted regression with 1000 bootstrap replicate weights estimated sociodemographically standardized prevalences and means. Bipolar-spectrum disorder was associated with higher scores on the six-item Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6; range 0-24; mean difference 1.32 points; 95% CI 0.34 to 2.29) and more sleep problems (prevalence difference 8.47 percentage points; 95% CI 0.43 to 16.52). Current smoking estimates were also higher (26.8% vs 19.3%; difference 7.49 percentage points; 95% CI -0.29 to 15.28), with a larger difference under the strict bipolar I/II definition after full sociodemographic adjustment. In the broad bipolar-spectrum comparison, smoking, distress, and sleep differences were attenuated and were not nominally significant after additional clinical adjustment. Recent activity was associated with higher positive mental health scores in both groups, while a differential association by diagnosis was not established. No group difference was detected in recent activity or diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions. The cross-sectional, self-reported design precludes causal inference. These results support integrated care addressing smoking, sleep, cardiometabolic assessment, and individualized physical activity.

papers.title: Associations between circadian-related behaviors and light exposure and depressive and anxiety symptoms among college students: A cross-sectional study of 10, 630 students from 4 universities.
papers.abstract: Depression and anxiety are highly prevalent among Chinese college students, whose circadian systems face chronotype-schedule mismatch, altered light exposure, and pervasive screen use; the joint associations of these factors with symptoms remain unclear. In a cross-sectional survey of 10,630 students from four Chinese universities, chronotype (rMEQ-5), social jetlag, daytime sunlight exposure, nighttime artificial light exposure (ALAN), and pre-sleep phone use were self-reported; depressive and anxiety symptoms were assessed with the PHQ-9 and GAD-7. Analyses comprised school fixed-effects linear regression with multiple imputation (m = 10), restricted cubic splines, latent profile analysis, and isotemporal substitution models. In fully adjusted single-exposure models, evening chronotype (β = 2.06, 95% CI 1.76-2.35), social jetlag (0.30/h), ALAN (0.22/SD), and pre-sleep phone use (0.33/30 min) were associated with higher PHQ-9 scores, and daytime sunlight (-0.11 per h/d) with lower scores (all P < 0.05); GAD-7 associations were directionally consistent at half the magnitude. Chronotype associations were nonlinear and concentrated in the evening range; the daylight association attenuated beyond ≈2.5 h/d. A long pre-sleep phone plus high social jetlag class scored 0.74 and 0.40 points higher than the high-daylight class. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; exposures were self-reported. Evening chronotype, social jetlag, nighttime light exposure, and pre-sleep screen use were associated with higher, and daytime sunlight with lower, symptom scores; the long pre-sleep phone plus high social jetlag class showed the highest scores; swapping 30 min of pre-sleep phone use for sunlight or sleep was associated with lower PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores, warranting prospective confirmation.

papers.title: How does circadian preference relate to post-traumatic stress and depressive symptoms in adolescents? A moderating role of gender.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to examine the associations between multidimensional circadian preference indicators and their profiles with PTSS and depressive symptoms, and investigate whether gender moderates these relationships. A cross-sectional school-based survey was conducted among 9305 adolescents from all 22 secondary schools in a county in northern China. Circadian preference were assessed using the Morningness-Eveningness-Stability-Scale improved (MESSi), comprising morning affect, eveningness, and distinctness. Depressive symptoms and PTSS were measured using the CES-D-10 and PCL-5, respectively. Latent profile analysis (LPA)was performed to identify circadian subtypes. Multivariable logistic regression and moderation analyses were conducted, adjusting for sociodemographic, health-related, and behavioral covariates. The prevalence of comorbid PTSS and depressive symptoms was 11.6%. LPA indentified three circadian profiles: Morning-Coordinated (4.37%), Intermediate-Stable (80.65%), and Evening-Fluctuating (14.98%). Compared with the Morning-Coordinated group, the Evening-Fluctuating group exhibited markedly elevated odds of comorbidity, isolated depression, and isolated PTSS. Higher morning affect was protective, whereas eveningness and distinctness were risk factors for all symptom outcomes. Gender significantly moderated these associations: the protective effect of morning affect and the adverse effects of eveningness and distinctness were consistently stronger among female adolescents. Circadian preference disruption, particularly the co-occurrence of evening preference and high diurnal fluctuation, is robustly associated with increased risks of PTSS and depressive symptoms in Chinese adolescents. Girls appear to be more vulnerable to the mental health consequences of circadian dysregulation. These findings highlight the importance of stabilizing daily routines and incorporating circadian health into school-based, gender-sensitive mental health interventions.

papers.title: Finding the weak spot: a new approach to locate unstable sites prone to conduction block in heterogeneous cardiac tissue.
papers.abstract: Safe and stable action potential propagation is crucial for the proper function of the heart. Altered propagation safety can lead to slow conduction and conduction block, the key ingredients of reentrant and potentially life-threatening arrhythmias. Hence, it is important to develop metrics to quantify the stability of conduction. The previously proposed safety factor, useful in computer simulations, is difficult to determine in real cardiac tissue. We hypothesized that unstable conduction, potentially prone to block, is sensitive to small perturbations of pacing and tested this in co-cultured strands of homozygous connexin 43 knock-out and heterozygous knock-out or wild-type murine ventricular cardiomyocytes grown on microelectrode arrays, and in corresponding computer simulations. The tissues were stimulated at a progressively increasing rate in the presence vs absence of stochastic or alternating variations of pacing cycle length. Variations of conduction times between adjacent electrodes were analyzed using principal components analysis. In 18 out of 19 cultured strands and in 10 out of 10 simulations, our approach correctly identified and predicted the location at which conduction block ultimately occurred already hundreds of beats and tens of seconds in advance. Interestingly, prediction was already possible in the absence of pacing variations, albeit with lower reliability. Finally, the site of slowest conduction was not necessarily the site of block. By permitting to identify sites of unstable conduction most prone to block occurs, our work may find translational applications in clinical cardiac electrophysiology during mapping and ablation procedures and open new avenues to explore innovative markers of conduction stability.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

papers.title: Neuronal and mitochondrial phenotypes in iPSC-derived bipolar disorder models with and without a family history of mitochondrial disease.
papers.abstract: Psychiatric disorders frequently accompany primary mitochondrial diseases (PMDs), suggesting shared biological pathways between mitochondrial function and psychiatric vulnerability. In this exploratory study, we investigated whether bipolar disorder (BD) occurring in the context of a family history of primary mitochondrial disease is associated with differences in neuronal and mitochondrial phenotypes. We generated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), neural progenitor cells (NPCs), and cortical neurons (CNs) from three non-psychiatric controls, three individuals with BD without a family history of mitochondrial disease, and three individuals with BD who did not themselves have mitochondrial disease but had relatives with clinically diagnosed mitochondrial (BD-FHMD). Our primary endpoints were distinguished network activity and cytosolic and mitochondrial Ca2+ dynamics, complemented by measurements of mitochondrial and cellular function and metabolomic profiles across differentiation. Across neurodifferentiation, we assessed neuronal network activity, calcium dynamics, mitochondrial and cellular health, and metabolomic signatures. BD neurons exhibited sustained hyperexcitability with increased firing and burst activity. In contrast, BD-FHMD neurons showed lower network activity with enhanced cytosolic calcium responses and prolonged mitochondrial calcium transients. BD-FHMD also exhibited stage-dependent mitochondrial alterations, while BD and BD-FHMD showed distinct developmental metabolic signatures. Together, these findings identify two distinct mitochondrial-associated phenotypes within BD. BD is characterized by a hyperexcitable neuronal phenotype associated with altered developmental metabolic programming, whereas BD-FHMD exhibits calcium dysregulation and altered mitochondrial developmental trajectories consistent with increased bioenergetic vulnerability. These findings suggest that BD occurring in the context of a family history of primary mitochondrial disease may be characterized by a distinct pattern of neuronal and mitochondrial dysfunction. Replication in larger, independently characterized cohorts will be important to determine whether this family-history-defined phenotype can contribute to biologically informed subtyping and therapeutic approaches in BD.

papers.title: Reported off-task thought and drowsiness differ in behavioral errors and prestimulus theta during sustained attention.
papers.abstract: Sustained attention can fail through a missed response or an incorrect choice, but it re-mains unclear whether these failures are associated with different subjective states. Twenty-eight adults performed a sustained two-choice letter-discrimination task while EEG was recorded. Thought probes asked whether they had been On-Task, Off-Task because of internal thoughts, or Drowsy. We analyzed behavioral responses and EEG activity during the three trials preceding each probe. Both Off-Task and Drowsiness reports were associated with poorer accuracy and slower correct responses than On-Task reports. However, their errors differed. Among inaccurate trials, the odds that an error was an omission rather than an incorrect-key response were higher for Off-Task than Drowsiness (OR = 3.04, 95% CI [1.48, 6.21]). Among trials with a valid response, the odds of an incorrect-key response were higher for Drowsiness than Off-Task (OR = 1.88, 95% CI [1.11, 3.19]). Prestimulus frontocentral theta power (4-7 Hz) was higher before Off-Task reports than before On-Task (+0.24 dB) or Drowsiness reports (+0.46 dB; Holm-adjusted p = 0.043 and 0.042, respectively). No state contrast survived Holm correction with individualized frequency bands. Similar reductions in overall accuracy concealed different error profiles. These findings sup-port considering off-task thought and drowsiness separately when examining how sustained attention fails.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology

papers.title: Egonol restores tamoxifen sensitivity via the miR-3529-5p-CLOCK axis in triple-negative breast cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective molecular targets and frequently develops therapeutic resistance, partly due to cancer stem-like cells (CSCs) characterized by high aldehyde dehydrogenase activity (ALDHhigh). We previously demonstrated that reduced expression of the circadian regulator CLOCK sustains stemness in murine TNBC-like cells. Here, we investigated the role of CLOCK in human TNBC cell line and explored natural compounds capable of restoring its expression. ALDHhigh populations isolated from MDA-MB-468 cells exhibited significantly decreased CLOCK expression mediated by 3' untranslated region (3' UTR)-dependent post-transcriptional repression. CLOCK overexpression restored estrogen receptor-α (ERα) expression and enhanced tamoxifen sensitivity, indicating that circadian regulation influences therapeutic responsiveness in TNBC. To identify CLOCK-stabilizing compounds, we performed high-throughput screening of 8008 medicinal plant extracts using a 3' UTR luciferase reporter system. S. obassia extract significantly increased CLOCK 3' UTR luciferase reporter activity without cytotoxicity. Bioactivity-guided fractionation identified egonol as the active component. Egonol suppressed miR-3529-5p expression, restored CLOCK and ERα levels, and enhanced tamoxifen-induced growth inhibition in ALDHhigh cells. These findings identify a previously unrecognized miR-3529-5p-CLOCK-ERα regulatory axis associated with therapeutic resistance in human TNBC cell line and suggest egonol as a potential circadian-modulating compound for restoring endocrine sensitivity.

papers.title: Linking ferroptosis to chronic sleep deprivation: emerging insights into mechanisms and interventions.
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for maintaining systemic homeostasis, facilitating tissue repair, and consolidating neural circuitry. In modern society, however, accelerated lifestyles and rising work pressures have made sleep deprivation (SD) a pressing public health concern. Recent studies increasingly link chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) to various neurological disorders. The precise mechanisms, however, are not fully understood. Notably, ferroptosis as a regulated form of cell death has emerged as a potential link between CSD and neurodegeneration. This narrative review critically synthesizes evidence linking CSD with ferroptosis, with particular emphasis on iron handling, lipid peroxidation, the system Xc - -GSH-GPX4 defense axis, mitochondrial/redox stress, and neuroinflammatory signaling. Furthermore, previous studies suggest that interventions such as ketogenic diets, ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, vitamin B6 and phytochemicals supplementation can modulate ferroptosis in CSD mouse model. Therefore, they may serve as potential nutritional and pharmacological therapeutic targets. However, current evidence remains predominantly preclinical, and many studies rely on ferroptosis-associated biomarkers rather than definitive causal tests. A deeper understanding of the mechanistic interplay between ferroptosis and CSD will not only advance our comprehension of CSD-induced neural impairment, but also provide a theoretical basis for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for sleep-related disorders.

papers.title: Audio large language models align with human neural responses during spoken-language comprehension.
papers.abstract: Audio large language models (audio LLMs) process continuous speech directly and transform it into progressively more abstract representations, providing a useful computational point of comparison with human spoken-language comprehension. Previous studies have reported model-brain correspondence for pretrained speech models and text-based language models, but it remains unclear which internal representations of audio LLMs are most closely associated with neural responses during online listening. We compared EEG responses from 41 native Mandarin listeners with internal representations from Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni, and Kimi-Audio in a Mandarin auditory semantic-violation paradigm that controlled sentence structure and event boundaries. We extracted speech-related and word-level semantic-update representations and quantified their incremental contributions to held-out EEG prediction beyond lower-level controls. Audio LLM representations improved EEG prediction beyond the acoustic envelope, phoneme onsets, and word onsets (Δr = 0.012, corrected P = 0.028). Prediction-score partitioning indicated that semantic violation primarily increased the overlap in EEG-predictive information between speech-related and semantic-update representations, rather than the unique contribution of either representation class. This pattern was relatively stable in Qwen2-Audio and Qwen2.5-Omni and directionally consistent, although statistically weaker, in Kimi-Audio. These findings provide component-level evidence that audio-conditioned model representations correspond to human neural responses during spoken-language comprehension, without implying mechanistic equivalence.

papers.title: Age-related reversal in the behavioral relevance of theta-alpha coupling during conflict processing.
papers.abstract: Cognitive aging is often characterized by slower responses during conflict processing, but the oscillatory coordination underlying this change remains poorly understood. We examined whether cross-frequency phase synchronization between theta and alpha activity is related to response conflict processing and whether its behavioral relevance changes across adulthood. N = 117 healthy adults aged 32-84 years performed a flanker task while an EEG was recorded. Theta-alpha phase-phase coupling was quantified as phase-locking value (PLV) across task-relevant time windows; time-frequency and source-level analyses characterized the underlying dynamics. Incongruent trials produced robust behavioral conflict, with lower accuracy and slower responses than congruent trials. Theta-alpha coupling showed a pronounced 1:1 structure across conditions, and was selectively stronger during incongruent trials. Time-frequency and source-level analysis provided complementary evidence of frontocentral theta engagement and alpha modulation in posterior and sensorimotor regions. Theta-alpha PLV at FCz during the target-processing window declined with age in incongruent trials, and its association with reaction time varied with age in the incongruent-trial analysis. Stronger coupling was associated with faster responses at younger ages, whereas the same coupling was associated with slower responses at older ages. A direct comparison did not establish that this age-dependent association differed between congruent and incongruent trials. These findings suggest that theta-alpha coupling is sensitive to response conflict and may contribute to the coordination of control-related and gating-related processes. Its age-related decline and changing association with response speed highlight the relevance of cross-frequency coordination for understanding cognitive aging.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Neurophysiology Alterations in Association with Aβ and Tau Pathology Across the Symptomatic Stages of Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau deposition drive Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, how these proteinopathies are linked to macroscopic neural activity alterations measured by electroencephalography (EEG) in symptomatic AD remains inadequately characterized. This study aims to investigate the associations between Aβ, tau, EEG neurophysiology, and cognition. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 73 MCI and AD participants, who underwent resting-state EEG, Aβ-PET, and tau-PET. EEG source analysis was performed to extract regional spectral power. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the associations of regional Aβ (quantified by SUVR), tau (binary classification), with EEG features, controlling for age, sex and education. Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was applied to investigate the relationships of EEG spectral power and global Aβ burden with cognitive performance. Elevated Aβ burden was associated with distinct regional spectral alterations. Specifically, higher Aβ SUVR was significantly correlated with increased theta power and decreased beta power in a subset of cortical regions. Tau positivity did not modulate the amyloid-theta association in any region, but attenuated the amyloid-beta association in a small set of parietal regions. We identified a localized pattern of Aβ-related neurophysiological dysfunction across the symptomatic stages of AD continuum, characterized by theta increases and beta decreases, supporting a robust association between Aβ burden and cortical neural slowing. The findings highlight the value of source-localized EEG power as a sensitive indicator of Aβ-associated network dysfunction in AD and underscore the potential of source-localized EEG as a complementary, non-invasive biomarker for assessing pathological burden and informing diagnostic strategies in AD.

papers.title: CMKLR1 contributes to diurnal variation in brain injury after cardiac arrest by promoting lactate production in microglia.
papers.abstract: Previously, the results of our clinical study have suggested that circadian rhythm have an impact on neurological outcomes following cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CA/CPR), but the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Here, using a mouse model of CA/CPR, we aimed to unravel the underlying mechanisms of the diurnal variation in CA/CPR-induced brain injury. The mice received five minutes of CA either in the active phase or in the inactive phase. To identify novel therapeutic targets for the impact of circadian rhythm on CA/CPR-induced brain injury, we applied high throughput RNA-seq analysis to profile mRNAs with differentially expression in the hippocampus of the two groups. Since it has been reported that CMKLR1 is beneficial for inhibiting neuroinflammation and improving neurological outcomes among many neurological diseases, we centered on this gene and clarified that its main cellular source is microglia. The correlation between CMKLR1 expression in hippocampus and neurological outcomes after CA/CPR was elucidated by CMKLR1 activation and knockout in microglia. The impact of CMKLR1 on microglial function, especially glucose metabolism, was clarified using BV2 microglia cell line by glucose uptake analysis, seahorse analysis and carbon 13 tracing. As a result, CA/CPR happening at active phase leads to better neurological outcomes with upregulation of microglial CMKLR1 in the hippocampus of mice. Our findings suggest that elevated microglial CMKLR1 expression in the hippocampus contributes to improved neurological outcomes after CA/CPR by promoting lactate production in microglia.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea: an overlooked challenge in the current NHS Strategy.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is common, frequently symptomatic, and closely associated with conditions already prioritised by the UK National Health Service (NHS), including obesity, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, cardiovascular disease, and stroke. Previous estimates suggest that approximately 8 million UK adults aged 30-69 years could have OSA, although the proportion remaining undiagnosed is uncertain. Evidence supports treatment benefits for daytime sleepiness, symptom burden, quality of life, driving safety, and blood pressure in some patients, but not a consistent reduction in major cardiovascular events. UK data indicate long diagnostic waits, regional variation, and gaps in follow-up. A proportionate NHS response should prioritise targeted case-finding within existing chronic-disease pathways, access to validated home-based diagnostics, specialist capacity for complex disease, and sustained treatment support. Implementation should be phased and evaluated prospectively for clinical outcomes, equity, workforce requirements, affordability, and budget impact.

papers.title: COP1 is a temperature-responsive switch in Arabidopsis.
papers.abstract: Temperature is molecular motion, but how living systems sense this is poorly understood. Many responses in plants integrate light and temperature signals, for example, via light receptors and the circadian clock. CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENESIS 1 (COP1) regulates light signaling and is necessary for responding to temperature. We show that COP1 acts as a temperature-dependent switch, becoming activated by a warm temperature-induced conformational change. An intramolecular Val-Pro (VP) motif binds to the active site of COP1 at low temperatures, preventing substrate docking. At warmer temperatures, the VP motif becomes detached, enabling client proteins to bind and be degraded. This discovery explains how plants are able to obtain a precise readout of temperature within a given climate range. Altering the binding of the VP motif is sufficient to adjust the temperature range within which the plant responds. This helps us understand how plants are able to adapt to different climates.

papers.title: Noninvasive Intracranial Compliance Monitoring Following Hand-Applied Photobiomodulation and Ultrasound in Fibromyalgia: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) is associated with chronic pain and altered neurophysiological regulation. This exploratory pilot study examined intracranial pulse waveform parameters and clinical outcomes following combined photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) and therapeutic ultrasound (TUS) applied bilaterally to the hands. Twenty women participated (FM, n = 10; healthy comparators, n = 10); both groups received 10 sessions over 5 weeks. Noninvasive measurements included waveform morphology, P2/P1 ratio, and time to peak. Pain intensity, Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores were also assessed. At baseline, participants with FM showed a higher proportion of P2 > P1 waveforms and longer time to peak than healthy participants. Following treatment, the FM group showed fewer P2 > P1 waveforms, shorter time to peak, and lower pain, functional impact, and sleep disturbance scores. The P2/P1 ratio did not change significantly. Without a sham-treated group, these findings indicate preliminary associations rather than treatment efficacy or causality.
