papers.title: Increasing Specialty Menopause Referrals for Premenopausal Breast Cancer Patients: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
papers.abstract: Premenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer often develop severe menopausal symptoms from chemotherapy and endocrine therapy, reducing quality of life (QoL) and contributing to early treatment discontinuation. Referral to specialty menopause care remains inconsistent. This project evaluated whether an interdisciplinary educational intervention, combined with a structured referral pathway to a specialty menopause care clinic, could improve provider confidence and increase referrals. The project was conducted at the Swedish Gynecology Specialty Center and Swedish Breast Medical Oncology Clinic. Oncology providers and menopause-certified gynecology clinicians participated in a 60-minute hybrid workshop addressing menopause management and referral processes. Pre- and post-intervention surveys assessed provider awareness and comfort. Referral volume was tracked across Baseline (January-April 2025), Early Implementation (April-October 2025), and Post-Implementation (October 2025-January 2026). Referrals increased from 22 (6.8/mo) at baseline to 104 (27.3/mo) post-implementation, representing a fourfold increase. Early implementation referrals (17.3/mo) suggested increased awareness contributed to uptake. Provider awareness of menopausal and sexual health issues rose from 80% to 100%, and comfort discussing these symptoms increased by 14%-16%. Patient surveys (n = 23) revealed a high symptom burden, including sleep disturbance (82%) and hot flashes (77%). Most patients (87.5%) found the specialty clinic helpful, and 95.7% intended to complete their endocrine therapy. An interdisciplinary educational intervention with a structured referral pathway significantly improved provider confidence and increased menopause specialty referrals. Integrating menopause expertise into oncology care is feasible and may enhance symptom management, treatment adherence, and QoL.

papers.title: Nutrition as a cross-cutting pillar of lifestyle medicine for frailty prevention and healthy aging in older adults.
papers.abstract: Frailty is a dynamic, multidimensional state of diminished physiologic reserve that increases vulnerability to stressors and predicts disability, hospitalization, and mortality in older adults. Nutrition is one of the six pillars of lifestyle medicine (alongside physical activity, restorative sleep, stress management, positive social connection, and avoidance of risky substances), an evidence-based framework for promoting health and preventing disease. In older adults, optimal energy, protein, and micronutrient intake supports muscle mass, functional capacity, and metabolic and cognitive resilience, whereas poor diet quality and undernutrition worsen sleep, stress physiology, and frailty trajectories. This mini-review synthesizes how nutrition interacts with each pillar of lifestyle medicine in older adults and considers implications for clinical practice and research. Nutrition emerges as a central determinant of healthy aging, directly influencing physiologic resilience and shaping the benefits of the other lifestyle medicine pillars in preserving strength, function, and independence.
papers.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

papers.title: Tumor incidence and mortality rates from the carcinogen N-methyl-N-nitrosurea vary by vendor in Siberian hamsters.
papers.abstract: N-Methyl-N-Nitrosourea (NMU) is a carcinogen used to induce tumors in mammary tissues in laboratory animals. We obtained NMU from Sigma-Aldrich (SA), The National Cancer Institute Carcinogen Repository (NCICR), and Toronto Research Chemicals, Inc. (TRC). NMU administered at 50 mg/kg from SA induced mammary epithelial tumors within 4-8 weeks. By contrast, the same dose of NMU obtained from NCICR failed to induce tumors in any of the animals despite monitoring them for over one year. All animals injected with the same dose of NMU from TRC either died or had to be euthanized by day 10 post-injection. After controlling for dose, route of administration, and age, we propose that vendor source might account for the variation in tumor incidence and mortality rate in Siberian hamsters.

papers.title: Interictal Electroencephalographic Characteristics of the Human Centromedian Thalamic Nucleus Recorded in Focal Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: The centromedian (CM) thalamic nucleus is critical in sleep-wake regulation and epileptic networks; yet its electroencephalography (EEG) characteristics remain incompletely understood. CM EEG across vigilance states and interictal epileptic discharges (IEDs) in focal epilepsy were investigated. Interictal stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from the CM and neighboring ventroposterior (VP) and ventrolateral (VL) nuclei were analyzed with synchronous cortical SEEG and scalp EEG during wakefulness, non-rapid eye movement sleep, rapid eye movement sleep, and spontaneous non-epileptic arousal. Spectral power was quantified across frequency bands. Sleep-related thalamic activities and thalamic IEDs were visually identified. SEEG data from 33 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy and 3 non-epileptic individuals were analyzed. CM exhibited continuous fast activity during wakefulness and delta/theta-dominant activity during sleep, confirmed by increased gamma-fast ripple power in wakefulness and enhanced delta/theta power in sleep (all p < 0.014). During spontaneous non-epileptic arousal, thalamic EEG changes preceded scalp EEG arousal (median 800 ms; interquartile range: 400-1500 ms). Four sleep-related thalamic EEG activities were reproducibly observed in non-epileptic individuals, supporting a potential physiological nature. Thalamic IEDs occurred in 36.4% of patients with focal epilepsy, invariably involved the CM. Thalamic IEDs were more frequent in extratemporal than temporal lobe epilepsy and were not associated with surgical outcome. CM SEEG demonstrates distinct, state-dependent electrophysiological dynamics across the sleep-wake cycle and preferential involvement in interictal epileptic activity compared with VL/VP nuclei. These findings lay the foundation for a thalamic EEG atlas and refine understanding of differential engagement of thalamic nuclei in epileptic networks.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: From attention capture to responsibility attribution: Public responses to AI discrimination crises.
papers.abstract: Understanding how publics respond to discrimination by artificial intelligence (AI) matters for organizations managing technology-related crises. Using the associative-propositional evaluation (APE) model as an organizing framework, this study reports two experiments comparing AI discrimination with executive discrimination. Study 1 (N = 148) used a controlled news scenario. AI discrimination produced higher corporate responsibility attribution, whereas executive discrimination produced lower corporate reputation and higher negative word-of-mouth (NWOM) intention; because the NWOM scale was only moderately reliable (α = 0.54, ω = 0.55), that result is reported as preliminary. Study 2 (N = 30) used electroencephalography (EEG) while participants viewed simulated social-media messages. AI discrimination elicited a larger P2 amplitude (dz = 0.60) and lower frontal-central theta-band activity (dz = -0.43) than executive discrimination, whereas the behavioral responsibility-attribution difference was small and not statistically significant (dz = 0.32, 95% CI [-0.05, 0.68]). Read together, the two studies show a separation between responsibility judgment and punishment-related responses: under the same actor cue, responsibility rose while punishment-related responses moved in the opposite direction, and the cue was registered within the first quarter-second of processing. This pattern constrains dual-process accounts of crisis response. The findings may inform, rather than prescribe, organizational communication and governance responses to discrimination crises.

papers.title: A collaborative network of bi-Mamba and CAFS for multi-task classification of unilateral lower limb.
papers.abstract: Accurate decoding of motor-related electroencephalography signals remains challenging in brain-computer interface research. To date, motor imagery of the upper limbs has been extensively investigated, while research on the lower limbs remains limited. Meanwhile, multiple tasks involving the unilateral lower limb (including motor imagery, motor execution, and motor observation for both the left and right lower limb) pose decoding challenges because these tasks activate similar brain regions (i.e., sensorimotor cortex), and contralateral cortex activation is closer to the brain's midline compared to the upper limbs. These challenges make classification challenging for existing deep learning models. To address the above problem, we proposed a collaborative network of bidirectional Mamba and convolutional attention feature selection (CN-BMCAFS) to classify multiple tasks of the unilateral lower limb. In CN-BMCAFS, a global temporal bidirectional Mamba module (GT Bi-Mamba) is employed to capture globally discriminative temporal features. The convolutional attention feature selection module (CAFS) is designed to capture informative local temporal features. The GT Bi-Mamba and CAFS are cascaded in a recurrent manner, enabling the combined advantage of GT Bi-Mamba capturing global temporal features while considering local temporal correlations and CAFS capturing local temporal features while considering global temporal correlations. The results demonstrated that CN-BMCAFS achieved the best performance in classification accuracy, with an accuracy improvement ranging from 1.79% to 14.5% compared to other models. Visualization results show that GT Bi-Mamba enhances the model's ability to accurately distinguish features among MI, ME, and MO, thereby improving decoding performance.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society

papers.title: Exploring the effect of attention on the acoustic change complex: cross-condition reliability and between-subject variability.
papers.abstract: The 'acoustic change complex' (ACC) auditory evoked potential shows promise as an objective measure of the neural capacity for sound discrimination. Given the ACC is increasingly proposed as a means to assess participants unable to respond behaviourally (e.g. infants with hearing loss), it is important to fully explore its objective nature. This study investigated whether the ACC response is modulated by attention. ACC responses were recorded via EEG from thirteen normal hearing adults (22-31 years), both with (Attend) and without (Ignore) a counting task designed to direct attention toward 1 kHz sound stimuli containing a 10% frequency change (2000 ms pre-transition duration; 128 trials). Statistical analyses were performed to assess condition effects, agreement between conditions, and variability of ACC measures. ACC waveforms showed no significant differences between Attend and Ignore conditions for N1 and P2 latencies, or for N1-P2 peak-to-peak amplitudes, and equivalence was demonstrated. Pairwise differences and Bland-Altman analyses showed good participant-level agreement between conditions. Intraclass correlation coefficients indicated good cross-condition reliability. Condition-independent coefficient of variation values indicated relatively low (9.5%, N1 latency; 6.4%, P2 latency) and high (45.7%, N1-P2 amplitude) between-subject variability. No attention-related differences in the ACC responses were detected, supporting further investigation of the ACC as an objective measure of auditory discrimination. Participant-level and group-level analyses demonstrated good agreement between Attend and Ignore conditions, suggesting that ACC measures are relatively robust to variations in attentional state. ACC latencies were relatively consistent across participants, whereas amplitudes showed greater variability.

papers.title: Clinical value of video monitoring in seizure classification and medication decision-making: A questionnaire-based study in outpatients with epilepsy.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the clinical value of ictal video monitoring in refining seizure classification and guiding antiseizure medication (ASM) decisions in outpatients with epilepsy, and to examine the concordance between eyewitness descriptions and objective video evidence. In this questionnaire-based, single-center study, 525 patients with epilepsy who attended the neurology outpatient clinic of West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between July and September 2025 were enrolled. A self-designed questionnaire was used to collect demographic information, medication history, seizure types, eyewitness descriptions, ictal video recordings, and diagnostic classifications before and after video review. Patients with ictal videos were grouped by recording modality: mobile phone recording, surveillance footage, and video-EEG (VEEG) monitoring. Initial classification was performed without video; a second classification was then performed with video when available. Classifications were independently reviewed once by an experienced epilepsy-specialist neurologist, with final adjudication by a senior physician in cases of disagreement.Categorical variables were compared using the χ2 test or Fisher's exact test when expected frequencies were < 5, with two-sided P < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Ictal video recordings were available for 159 of 525 patients (30.3 %). Among the 159 patients with complete pre- and post-video diagnostic records, diagnostic revision occurred in 32 patients (20.1 %). The most common revision pathway was bilateral tonic-clonic seizure of unknown onset (BTC) to focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizure (FBTC), accounting for 46.9 % (15/32) of all revisions. A determinate final seizure classification (focal or generalized) was more frequent in patients with ictal videos than in those without (96/159 [60.4 %] vs 121/366 [33.1 %], P < 0.001). ASM regimens were changed based on video evidence in 19/159 patients (11.9 %), and 16 patients required subsequent readjustment. Diagnostic revision rates were 15.2 % (19/125) for mobile phone recordings, 36.8 % (7/19) for surveillance footage, and 40.0 % (6/15) for VEEG monitoring. Diagnostic revision was significantly associated with ASM regimen changes (χ2 = 4.22, P = 0.040). An eyewitness was present at consultation for 512/525 patients (97.5 %), and the diagnostic concordance rate between eyewitness descriptions and video evidence was 89.9 %. Ictal video recording was associated with clinically meaningful revision of seizure classification and influenced ASM decisions in outpatients with epilepsy, with higher diagnostic yield observed for more professional recording modalities. Video evidence may help correct classification bias arising from reliance on verbal history, particularly in identifying focal onset.

papers.title: Epilepsy Online Social Support: Characterizing topics and challenges shared in the r/Epilepsy community.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is one of the most common neurological conditions, and people living with epilepsy (PLWE) often use social media as a resource. However, a comprehensive understanding of the topics represented in epilepsy-specific communities where PLWE may be more honest is essential to designing better technologies to address epilepsy self-management. To understand the main topics and concerns of PLWE, we collected 23,945 r/Epilepsy subreddit posts and performed topic modeling, thematic analysis, and psycholinguistic analysis. We found five major themes among those topics: symptoms and triggers (e.g., mental health and memory, sleep/nocturnal, and photosensitivity), treatment and healthcare experience (e.g., medication, understanding epilepsy), daily functions (e.g., perceived level of independence and finances), seizure activity (e.g., auras and ictal symptoms), and support for PLWE (assisting PLWE and support for PLWE). We highlight the top psycho-linguistic characteristics of posts across different topics. Our contributions include providing an understanding of the challenges of an online epilepsy community and their social support needs, and implications for designing technologies.

papers.title: A VPS4A Microtubule-Interacting and Trafficking Domain Variant in a Child With Hypomyelination and Developmental Regression: A Case Report With Features of CIMDAG Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy in infancy has a broad differential diagnosis. Heterozygous variants in VPS4A, an endosomal sorting complexes required for transport-associated AAA-ATPase, have been reported in CIMDAG (cerebellar hypoplasia-cataracts-impaired intellectual development-congenital microcephaly- dystonia-dyserythropoietic anemia-growth retardation) syndrome, a multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder with variable systemic involvement. A 14-month-old girl presented with inability to crawl or walk and delayed milestones. Examination showed a head circumference of 43.5 cm, a depressed nasal bridge, bilateral 4th-5th toe clinodactyly, motor delay, and hypotonia. Metabolic screening and targeted genetic tests were nondiagnostic. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed diffuse deficient myelination, a thin corpus callosum, optic nerve hypoplasia, and basal ganglia signal abnormalities. At 2 years 7 months, the child re-presented with loss of independent sitting and speech, tremor, and epileptiform electroencephalography abnormalities. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging showed persistent deficient myelination despite mild interval progression of myelination. Echocardiography showed moderate mitral regurgitation and a patent foramen ovale. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous VPS4A variant, NM_013245.3:c.217T>G (p.Tyr73Asp), reported as absent from population databases and previously unreported at the time of testing. Maternal testing was negative; paternal testing was unavailable. The laboratory classified the variant as a variant of uncertain significance. The clinical and imaging findings overlap with the VPS4A-associated CIMDAG spectrum. This case describes a candidate heterozygous microtubule-interacting and trafficking domain variant in a child with hypomyelination and regression; its contribution to the phenotype remains unconfirmed.

papers.title: [Prevalence of burnout syndrome in resident physicians in a university hospital: a cross-sectional study of personal, work and lifestyle factors].
papers.abstract: Burnout syndrome (BS) is a relevant occupational health issue among medical residents, particularly in contexts of high clinical and academic demands. Its impact affects both the mental health of the resident and the quality of medical training and patient care. To determine the prevalence of burnout syndrome in medical residents at a university hospital and to explore associated sociodemographic, occupational and lifestyle factors, with special emphasis on educational implications. A cross-sectional, observational, descriptive-analytical study was conducted using an anonymous, self-administered online questionnaire. The Spanish-validated version of the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS) was used, along with items on sociodemographic, occupational, and lifestyle variables. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS v19, with descriptive and inferential tests. A total of 68 residents participated (response rate: 35%). High emotional exhaustion was observed in 61.7% of participants (n=42), high depersonalization in 66,1% (n=45), and low personal accomplishment in 26,5% (n=18). The overall prevalence of burnout was 60.3%. Burnout was more frequent in surgical specialties and in residents reporting poor sleep and physical inactivity. Significant associations were found between male gender and depersonalization (p=0.006), and between perceived social support and personal accomplishment (p <0.05). Burnout syndrome is highly prevalent among medical residents and is associated with both personal and professional factors. Preventive and educational strategies should be integrated into medical training to promote emotional wellbeing and professional resilience.
keywords: Inventario de Burnout de Maslach – Encuesta para servicios humanos

papers.title: Detection of linear dependencies in EEG oscillatory sources via PARALIND and block-term decomposition: A comparative study.
papers.abstract: Narrowband oscillatory rhythms in electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are fundamental signatures of neural dynamics, crucial for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and monitoring neurological disorders. While traditionally detected and analyzed via Independent or Principal Component Analysis in the time-space domain, tensor decomposition in the time-space-frequency domain offers superior resolution. The CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) model is widely used for this purpose due to itssimplicity and interpretability. However, it often fails to resolve rhythms or requires excessive components when source collinearity exists (i.e., a situation where oscillatory rhythms share characteristics across temporal, spatial, or frequency modes), leading to instability and increased computational complexity.Approach: This study evaluates two alternative tensor decomposition models - Parallel Profiles with Linear Dependencies (PARALIND) and Block-Term Decomposition (BTD) - which explicitly accommodate linear dependencies among latent components. We compared these models against CP using simulated EEG data with known ground-truth structures and real-world recordings.Main results: PARALIND and BTD achieved interpretability comparable to CP while providing more stable factor estimates at moderate noise levels in simulated data, although both models struggled to identify the true latent structure under challenging conditions. Overall, when their modelling assumptions were satisfied, PARALIND and BTD successfully disentangled complex, overlapping neural sources that CP struggled to isolate. In real data, both models recovered a latent structure similar to that identified by CP, but with fewer loadings. Following the principle of parsimony, PARALIND and BTD may therefore be preferable in this setting.Significance: By overcoming the collinearity limitations inherent in CP decomposition, these findings establish a more reliable framework for neurophysiologically interpretable tensor decomposition of EEG signals. While clinical translation was not evaluated in this work, this methodological advance provides a foundation for future research aimed at enhancing BCI stability and investigating biomarkers of neurological conditions.

papers.title: MSTA-CNN an ultra-lightweight multi-scale temporal-spatial attention convolutional neural network for high-performance P300 spellers.
papers.abstract: Efficient P300 detection in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) remains a challenge due to low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the high computational cost of existing deep learning models, which limits their deployment in real-time applications. To address these issues, we propose MSTA-CNN, an ultra-lightweight multi-scale temporal-spatial attention convolutional neural network with only 3,153 trainable parameters. By synergizing depthwise separable convolutions for hierarchical feature extraction with a dual-branch attention mechanism designed to dynamically re-weight informative channels and temporal segments MSTA-CNN achieves robust end-to-end learning from minimally preprocessed EEG data. Extensive evaluations on the BCI Competition II Dataset IIb and III Dataset II demonstrate state-of-the-art character recognition accuracy, reaching 98% at 15 sequences and an average of 97.5% across subjects. Notably, the model yields a practical information transfer rate (ITR) of 13.72 bits/min, significantly outperforming baseline methods in critical low-repetition scenarios while being 10-50× lighter. The learned representations align closely with P300 neurophysiology, as evidenced by spatial importance maps and t-SNE visualizations. MSTA-CNN establishes a new benchmark for efficient P300 spellers, paving the way for portable, high-speed BCI systems for individuals with severe motor disabilities.

papers.title: Temporal-context learning for subject-independent sleep staging with non-contact multi-frequency radar.
papers.abstract: Contactless radar may support unobtrusive sleep monitoring, but reliable five-stage evaluation requires participant-isolated testing and a clear assessment of the contribution of model components. The analysis included all 32 overnight recordings (33 964 labelled 30 s epochs) in the PhysioNet Sleep Bioradiolocation Database. Eight documented I/Q channel pairs spanning 3.6-4.0 GHz underwent complex clutter suppression, phase demodulation, fixed 0.05-0.70 Hz zero-phase filtering and resampling to 10 Hz. A 266 342-parameter composite network combined a shared one-dimensional encoder, cross-frequency contrastive initialization, quality-conditioned frequency fusion and a bidirectional gated recurrent unit over nine epochs. Eight deterministic folds each used 24 training, four validation and four held-out test participants, so every participant was tested once. Primary outcomes were participant-level five-stage macro-F1, balanced accuracy and Cohen's kappa. The full network achieved accuracy 0.434, macro-F1 0.376 (95% confidence interval 0.344-0.409), balanced accuracy 0.432 (0.405-0.457) and kappa 0.271 (0.235-0.308). Removing temporal context reduced macro-F1 by 0.072 (0.050-0.095), whereas neither contrastive initialization nor learned fusion showed an incremental held-out benefit. An independently trained early-fusion CNN-BiGRU achieved macro-F1 0.296. The participant-isolated evaluation identifies temporal context as the main contributor among the assessed components and provides a reproducible reference for future radar-based sleep-staging studies.

papers.title: Nursing Interventions for Pain and Sleep Management in Cancer Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: To map nursing interventions for pain and sleep disturbance among adults receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors and identify assessment and research gaps. A scoping review. Eligible sources were charted using a standardized form and descriptively synthesized by intervention type, outcome, study design and evidence stream. PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature were searched on 30 November 2025 for English-language sources published from 1 January 2019 to 30 November 2025. We included 10 sources: one randomized clinical trial, four systematic reviews, three of which included meta-analysis, three observational studies, one mixed-methods study and one structured clinical perspective/review. Four sources provided direct evidence from populations receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, whereas six provided potentially transferable evidence from broader oncology populations. Electronic patient-reported outcome monitoring produced promising findings in one immune checkpoint inhibitor trial. Broader oncology evidence identified potentially transferable pain-management approaches. Two primary studies explicitly reported sleep-related findings, but neither reported using a dedicated, validated sleep-specific instrument. Sleep-related content within broader symptom or quality-of-life assessments was distinguished from dedicated sleep assessment. No included ICI-specific nursing intervention primarily targeted insomnia. Direct evidence for nurse-led pain and sleep interventions during immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment remains limited. Findings from broader oncology populations should not be interpreted as evidence of effectiveness in this population. Oncology nurses may consider assessing pain and sleep separately. Future research should incorporate validated sleep measures and explore interventions tailored to patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. The study addressed the limited nursing evidence for managing pain and sleep disturbance during immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment. The main findings were the scarcity of direct intervention evidence and the absence of validated sleep-specific assessment. The findings will inform oncology nurses, researchers and services caring for adults receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews. No patients or members of the public were involved in this review, which was based on published evidence.

papers.title: Evaluating Age-Related Motor System Changes Using Gait as a Functionally Relevant Marker.
papers.abstract: Aging causes gait and mobility decline, which often precedes cognitive impairment and dementia. Biological "age gaps" (the difference between biological and chronological age) are traditionally measured using neuroimaging and electroencephalography, quantified gait metrics have not been used for this purpose. We hypothesize that specific gait metrics can effectively quantify biological aging and predict future cognitive impairment risk. We analyzed gait data from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, a population-based cohort in Olmsted County, MN. Participants without known gait disorder, recruited between 2007 and 2025, were included. We used these data to develop a machine learning-based age prediction model. This gait-based age prediction model was used to devise the "gait age gap," a quantified metric of gait abnormality defined as the difference between age as predicted by gait performance ("gait age") and chronological age. We used the gait age gap to evaluate the risk of future cognitive impairment. We analyzed 19,637 walk trials from 5,794 unique participants (49% female), with a mean age of 78 (±8) years. Gait age was primarily driven by changes in measures of stability. A larger gait age gap was associated with impaired cognitive and functional status. In longitudinal analysis, each gait age gap year exceeding chronological age increased the risk of converting from a normal to cognitively impaired (CI) state by 7% per year. Gait age gap outperformed baseline velocity in distinguishing normal from CI groups and was associated with future risk of conversion from normal to a CI state hazard ratio = 1.07 (95% CI 1.03-1.13) for gait age gap vs hazard ratio = 0.99 (95% CI 0.98-1.00) for velocity. The gait age gap is a functionally relevant marker of age-related motor system changes that quantifies deviations from expected gait performance for a given chronological age. It is associated with a higher risk of future cognitive impairment among cognitively normal individuals. This study includes a relatively homogeneous cohort of predominantly Caucasian participants. To assess generalizability and the trajectory of motoric aging across sociodemographic groups, these findings need to be replicated in diverse cohorts. Wearable sensor technologies could also make such measures more scalable.

papers.title: Terahertz coal-rock identification method based on multi-representation feature fusion.
papers.abstract: To improve the classification performance of coal-rock identification by enhancing spectral feature representation, this study proposes a terahertz-based multi-representation feature fusion model, termed THz-CVFusionNet. Terahertz time-domain signals of six types of coal-rock samples were acquired using a terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) system. After frequency-domain transformation, the 0.1-2.0 THz range was selected for spectral analysis, and the effective absorption coefficient was extracted as the key feature parameter. A dual-branch network was developed to integrate complementary spectral representations. The 1D-CNN branch captures local spectral patterns from effective absorption coefficient sequences. The spectral sequences were further transformed into two-dimensional GAF representations for global correlation modeling using a 2D Vision Transformer. Feature-level fusion was then used to combine the two branches for classification. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieved accuracy, macro-precision, macro-recall, and macro-F1 score values above 97%, outperforming several mainstream models. These results demonstrate the potential of THz-TDS combined with feature fusion for accurate coal-rock identification.

papers.title: Testing for interactions in multivariate data.
papers.abstract: Factorial designs are a mainstay of the scientific paradigm, allowing the effects of multiple experimental factors and their interactions to be efficiently studied within a single experiment. In brain imaging, however, multivariate data analyses commonly proceed using multivariate decoding and we argue that the standard "difference of accuracies" test is not a true test of interactions. To remedy this situation we propose an encoding method based on a Bayesian multivariate linear model which is ideally suited to the factorial analysis of such data. We show how it can be used to test for multivariate main effects and interactions using data from EEG studies of reward learning and declarative memory. This approach additionally allows for null hypotheses to be accepted and allows one to infer whether multivariate effects are driven by collections of univariate effects or voxel dependencies. We also propose that those wishing to pursue tests for interactions using decoding methods use an "accuracy of differences" test.

papers.title: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel.
papers.abstract: Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae, reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore-lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Making sleep illegal: behavioral health impacts of public sleeping bans and proposed alternatives.
papers.abstract: In 2024, the Supreme Court ruled in the City of Grants Pass vs Johnson that local towns and municipalities may ban people from sleeping in public places, overturning a lower-court precedent that previously deemed this cruel and unusual punishment. This position paper sought to identify effective interventions for addressing homelessness and emphasize the implications of legislature on sleep and public health outcomes. As this is a policy position paper, the opinions listed in this report have been informed by existing evidence. We provide policy recommendations for research-supported approaches addressing homelessness. Successful interventions for homelessness included those that focused on providing support and increasing resources, such as the development of Safe Sleeping Zones in California, or providing individuals with housing subsidies, income assistance, or support in finding rentals. We provide the following policy recommendations for legislators: increased federal funding/incentives for unsheltered homelessness programs, a greater allocation of the federal budget attributed to supportive services, and increased legislation for homelessness prevention. We suggest a shift in focus on implementing more empowerment and supportive-based approaches as opposed to punitive approaches. Investing in homelessness prevention efforts has yielded long-term societal-level financial and economic benefits.

papers.title: Two minds, one body: neural correlates of processing of We-information during shared control over a humanoid robot.
papers.abstract: When speaking about the self, we typically think about 'I' or 'Me'. However, our relations with other people are also a critically important aspect of our self, forming our 'We'. In the current study, we investigated processing of information about the We during joint control over a single body. While naturally such a case occurs among the conjoint twins, we reconstructed such a situation by allowing two people to share control over a single humanoid robot. Using EEG, we investigated which neurocognitive processes are affected by providing We-information, i.e. information that conveys knowledge about properties at the group-level, while being uninformative about the individuals. We found that processing of We-information engages a cascade of processes, as indexed by various event-related potentials (ERPs), involving perception (P1, N1 and P2p), action selection (N2), working memory (P3b) and response preparation (contingent negative variation, CNV). We-information also modulates perception and processing of the subsequent information about the robot's target position, as indicated by modulation of similar ERPs (P1, N2 and P3b). Moreover, we found that We-information can affect dynamic allocation of covert attention towards the side of the partner controlling the other side of the robot. Overall, our results show that processing of information about the We can have a widespread influence on cognition, similarly to processing information about the self. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.
papers.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences

papers.title: Patterns of Non-Prescribed Modafinil Use as a Cognitive Enhancer Among University Students in the UK.
papers.abstract: Modafinil is a stimulant drug that is primarily prescribed for the management of the sleep disorder narcolepsy. Approximately 10% of UK university students use it as a cognitive enhancer (CE) to help with their studies, but there has been limited research aimed at trying to understand this statistic. We surveyed students who are using modafinil as a cognitive enhancer, with the aim of understanding the detailed patterns of modafinil use. Students were using modafinil as a cognitive enhancer in the mistaken belief that it was illegal to do so, but unconcerned by that legal status or the side effects they experienced, believing that it is effective as a cognitive enhancer. Average length of modafinil use was 11 months, obtained from online pharmacies and with modest doses taken. Modafinil use was planned and strategic, aimed at improving focus and concentration with limited appetite for any sort of intervention by the student's university. However some expressed concern about addiction and dependence, and there was concern about long-term effects. UK university students are using modafinil as a cognitive enhancer in a stable and planned but unregulated way.

papers.title: Fast-Gelling, Adhesive, and Conductive Epidermal Electrode for Accurate Physiological Signal Monitoring and Real-Time Brain-Controlled Drone Flight.
papers.abstract: Conductive hydrogel electrodes are vital components for achieving human-machine interfaces. However, the inherent trade-off between high conductivity and favorable mechanical/adhesive properties remains a significant challenge for hydrogel-based epidermal electrodes. Here, we developed a multifunctional MXene/WPU/PAA (MWA) hydrogel electrode that combines robust mechanical properties, strong adhesion, and excellent conductivity. The introduced MXene nanosheets can induce free-radical polymerization, resulting in fast gelation (<5 min) at room temperature. Theoretical analyses reveal that MXene nanosheets form abundant hydrogen bonds with polymer chains, thus enhancing the cross-linking density and mechanical strength of the hydrogel electrode. The MWA hydrogel can form a stable skin-electrode interface, enabling high-fidelity multimodal physiological signal monitoring. Specifically, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for sEMG reached 36.0 dB, while the SNR for ECG was 30.1 dB, outperforming the Ag/AgCl electrodes. The MWA hydrogel exhibits outstanding adhesion under repeated cycles and simulated sweat conditions, reaching 94.2 and 55.5 kPa, respectively. Furthermore, the MWA hydrogel electrode demonstrates precise scalp EEG monitoring, enabling wireless drone flight control via real-time brainwave decoding. This work provides insight into MXene-polymer interactions and demonstrates the applicability of the developed electrode to brain-computer interface applications.

papers.title: Feasibility of Using Consumer-Grade Wearables Among Adolescents Presenting for Specialty Concussion Care: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Autonomic dysfunction is common after concussion and may be compounded by inactivity. Accordingly, physical activity progression is an important component of concussion rehabilitation. Fitbit devices can provide objective longitudinal data on physical activity, physiologic response to activity, and sleep. However, participants must have adequate adherence to device wear to provide accurate data. The threshold for adequate adherence may change based on the research question, making it important to understand how adherence changes across different thresholds. Furthermore, it is unclear how much staff support (ie, reminders) may be required to maintain an adequate level of adherence. This study aimed to (1) evaluate adherence to Fitbit device wear during daytime and nighttime using 3 different thresholds (50%, 75%, and 90% wear time) over 13 weeks in adolescents presenting for specialty concussion care and (2) report the number of reminders required to achieve the observed level of adherence. A total of 80 adolescents were recruited from a specialty concussion clinic. Participants were asked to wear a Fitbit Sense 2 device day and night for 1 year. We analyzed data collected during the first 13 weeks. For each threshold, a day or night was considered valid if the percentage of minutes with recorded heart rate data was greater than or equal to the defined threshold. We fit 2 robust linear mixed-effects models with number of valid days or valid nights as the outcome, a fixed effect for time (week), a fixed effect for threshold (50%, 75%, and 90%), a time-by-threshold interaction, and a random slope and intercept for each participant. We also calculated the percentage of participants who required a reminder from the study team to wear the device and/or synchronize it and the average number of manual reminders sent per participant across the study period. A total of 70 participants were included in the analyses. Over 13 weeks, adolescents had average daily adherence ranging from 3.0 (SD 0.7) to 4.4 (SD 0.8) days/wk and average nightly adherence ranging from 3.6 (SD 0.7) to 3.9 (SD 0.7) nights/wk. Across all thresholds, adherence was highest during the first week. The number of valid wear days (β=-0.2; P<.001) and nights (β=-0.2; P<.001) decreased each week, regardless of the adherence threshold used. A total of 50 of 70 (71%) participants required at least 1 manual reminder from the study team. We found that adolescents presenting for specialty concussion care had adequate adherence to Fitbit device wear over 13 weeks. Approximately three-quarters of the participants required at least 1 reminder from the study team. This suggests that collecting longitudinal data with a Fitbit device is feasible in adolescents presenting for specialty concussion care but that reminders are needed to promote adherence.

papers.title: German wine and respiration: Remarks on the discovery, properties and significance of the Bötzinger complex.
papers.abstract: The Bötzinger complex (BötC) comprises a distinct bilateral group of interneurons that are active during the expiratory phase of the respiratory cycle, located in the rostral medulla ventral to the compact formation of the nucleus ambiguus. It was named after the bottles of wine served at the conference dinner of an international meeting held in Germany in 1980, where the first electrophysiological data describing these neurons were presented. In cats, BötC neurons predominantly exhibit an augmenting (E-Aug) firing pattern, whereas in rats E-Aug and E-Dec (decrementing expiratory) patterns are observed. Both subtypes issue axons that often extensively arborise on both sides of the medulla, forming inhibitory glycinergic and/or GABAergic synapses with inspiratory neurons of the dorsal and ventral respiratory groups. Additionally, E-Aug neurons project to the spinal cord and inhibit phrenic motoneurons. These properties contrast with those of another group of bulbospinal expiratory neurons in the caudal medulla, which do not issue medullary axon collaterals and are excitatory. BötC neurons regulate the interval during which inspiratory neurons remain silent and contribute to synchronisation of respiratory activity across both sides of the lower brainstem. Recent in vivo, reduced-preparation and in silico studies indicate that they also contribute to respiratory rhythmogenesis through mutual inhibitory synaptic interactions with the pre-Bötzinger complex. This review provides the history of the discovery and naming of the BötC and a detailed discussion of the properties of BötC neurons, including their location, morphology, afferent and efferent axonal projections, synaptic connectivity and functional role.

papers.title: Social Determinants of Health and Long-Term, Device-Based Sleep Health.
papers.abstract: Prior research on social determinants of health (SDOH) and sleep health has largely relied on subjective sleep measures, primarily self-reported sleep duration. Evidence remains limited on the associations between SDOH and wearable-derived long-term sleep patterns in large-scale populations. To examine how SDOH (overall and by domain) are associated with long-term, wearable-derived sleep duration and variability. This cross-sectional study included participants from the All of Us Research Program enrolled between 2018 and 2023 who contributed at least 180 days of wearable data, including pre-enrollment historical records, and completed the SDOH survey. Data analysis was conducted from September 2025 to June 2026. Measures of overall and domain-specific SDOH, including social and community context, economic stability, neighborhood environment, and health care access and quality, were derived from validated surveys and standardized to z scores. Mean daily sleep duration (in minutes) and day-to-day sleep duration SD across all available days were calculated from device-estimated main sleep episodes. Among 12 403 participants (mean [SD] age, 57.8 [15.2] years; 8719 female [70.3%]; 10 946 White [88.3%] and 1457 members of minority racial groups [11.7%]; 756 Hispanic [6.1%]), 9052 individuals (73.0%) had a college degree or above, with a mean (SD) sleep duration of 406.1 (44.9) minutes and a mean (SD) sleep duration SD of 76.9 (20.6) minutes. Participants were monitored for a median (range) of 982 (180 to 4133) days. Compared with participants in the lowest SDOH tertile, those in the highest tertile (indicating more favorable social and structural conditions) had 5.82 minutes (95% CI, 3.84 to 7.80 minutes) longer sleep duration and 4.79 minutes (95% CI, -5.69 to -3.89 minutes) lower sleep duration SD in the fully adjusted model. When examining individual SDOH domains, economic stability showed the strongest associations with mean sleep duration (eg, 10.70 minutes; 95% CI, 5.30 to 16.10 minutes) and sleep duration SD (eg, -8.70 minutes; 95% CI, -11.20 to -6.26 minutes). Limited subgroup heterogeneity in the association was observed across age, sex, race, and ethnicity. In this study, more favorable SDOH conditions were associated with longer and more regular habitual sleep duration over the long term, emphasizing the importance of social and structural factors when evaluating sleep health.

papers.title: Body recomposition in adults: mechanisms, modulators, and practical algorithms for simultaneous skeletal muscle mass gain and fat mass loss.
papers.abstract: Body recomposition is the concurrent increase in fat-free mass (FFM) or skeletal muscle mass and decrease in fat mass (FM) within the same intervention period. Although hypertrophy is commonly pursued in energy surplus and FM loss in energy deficit, controlled trials indicate that recomposition can occur when progressive resistance training (PRT), adequate protein intake, and an appropriate energy prescription are combined. We conducted a structured narrative review of randomised trials, meta-analyses, and selected mechanistic studies in adults, with emphasis on FFM, FM, strength, and performance outcomes. Device heterogeneity was considered when interpreting evidence, with greatest weight placed on four-compartment and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) outcomes. PRT combined with higher protein intake, typically ~1.6-2.4 g/kg/day and higher relative intakes during energy restriction or leanness, is the most consistent strategy for recomposition. Effects are largest in untrained individuals and those with higher adiposity, smaller in trained or lean athletes, and still feasible in older adults when anabolic resistance is addressed with supervised PRT and sufficient protein. Moderate deficits, carbohydrate allocation around key sessions, sleep, and recovery support FFM retention or accretion while facilitating FM loss. Practical applications: Programmes should pair progressive overload with protein-centred diets, modest energy deficits, and periodic monitoring of body composition and performance. Body recomposition is feasible but context-dependent; expected changes are generally modest in trained or lean populations and require individualised adjustment.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

papers.title: When Eating Organizes the Day: Food Chronocare Among Socioeconomically Vulnerable Families of Children and Adolescents With Autism and Other Neurodevelopmental Conditions in Northeastern Brazil.
papers.abstract: To understand, within the analytical scope of this article, how parents and caregivers organize and interpret the eating rhythms of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and/or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in relation to sleep, school, medication, behavior, sensory needs, and food selectivity. An explanatory sequential mixed methods study was conducted in three municipalities in northeastern Brazil. The quantitative phase included 128 families of children and adolescents with ASD and/or ADHD, including co-occurring conditions. The qualitative phase included interviews with 35 parents or primary caregivers representing 37 children and adolescents, analyzed through an interpretive thematic approach. Findings were integrated to examine convergences, complementarities, and mixed-methods interpretations. Ninety-four participants (73.4%) presented four or more of eight caregiver-reported food selectivity manifestations. A higher manifestation burden was associated with the need for help or supervision during meals (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] = 1.43; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.10-1.87), sleep difficulties on ≥ 8 days (aPR = 1.45; 95% CI: 1.08-1.95), and hypersensitivity reactions on ≥ 8 days (aPR = 1.88; 95% CI: 1.28-2.75). Qualitative findings showed how feeding was coordinated with sensory predictability, medication, school routines, sleep, nighttime hunger, and caregiver rest. Integration indicated that eating times were interconnected with other temporal and relational demands of family care. The integrated findings informed the development of food chronocare as a provisional interpretive concept that captures the family caregiving work through which eating rhythms are coordinated with sensory needs and the broader temporal demands of family life, schooling, medication use, and sleep among children and adolescents with autism and other neurodevelopmental conditions.
authors: Maria da Conceição Dos Santos Oliveira Cunha
papers.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

papers.title: The effect of listening to Qur'an on quality of life and sleep quality in breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effect of listening to Qur'an on quality of life and sleep quality in women undergoing chemotherapy for breast cancer. This randomized controlled trial used an open-label design at the participant level, with blinded statistical analysis. Participants were assigned using block randomization to either a Qur'an listening group (QLG) or a control group (CG). During each chemotherapy session, the QLG listened through headphones to a standardized recording of Surah Yasin played on a music player and repeated until the chemotherapy session was completed. The intervention was administered once every 21 days for a total of four sessions, while the CG received standard care only. Data were collected at four time points (T1-T4) using a Breast Cancer Patient Information Form, the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30), Version 3.0, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Analyses were performed using SPSS 26. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for several EORTC QLQ-C30 functional and symptom domains after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Global quality of life also showed a significant Group × Time interaction (p = 0.008), indicating different patterns of change between the QLG and CG across the four measurement points. Between-group differences in global quality of life were significant at T2 and T3. For sleep quality, the Group × Time interaction for PSQI total scores was significant after Holm correction (p < 0.001), and PSQI scores were significantly lower in the QLG than in the CG at T4 (p < 0.001). Qur'an listening during chemotherapy was associated with changes in patient-reported quality of life and sleep quality among women with breast cancer. Given the study limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger randomized controlled trials.Trial registrationNCT06893770.

papers.title: Sleep inertia takes center stage as a shared feature in central disorders of hypersomnolence.
From Sleep Awareness to Sleep Stewardship.
Side-to-side and other complex head movements as ictal signs in epilepsy: A video-EEG case series and review of literature.
papers.abstract: Side-to-side head shaking is often considered a distinctive clinical sign that differentiates functional seizures from epileptic seizures; however, it may also occur as an ictal phenomenon in focal epilepsy. We retrospectively reviewed all video-telemetry reports of patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing presurgical evaluation between 2015 and 2025. All reports were electronically screened for mentioning side-to-side or other complex head movements and the video-EEG of these patients was reviewed and included if associated with ictal EEG changes. Seventeen patients were identified who experienced 631 seizures in total, 201 of which included such movements (median: 2 per patient, range: 1-160). One patient (No. 5) accounted for 79% of these events and represented an outlier. Head movements were predominantly horizontal (93.5%), followed by mixed (5%) and rotatory (1.5%). While small-amplitude movements predominated overall, larger amplitudes were more frequent after excluding the outlier case. In six patients, head movements were the initial observed feature of seizure semiology and typically represented a brief component of the seizure, although prolonged in the outlier case. Interrater agreement ranged from fair to good across semiological variables. Presumed epileptogenic zones were heterogenous, including frontal, temporal, anterior quadrant, and hemispheric regions. Ictal side-to-side and other complex head movements can occur in focal epilepsies but lack localizing or lateralizing value. They likely reflect seizure propagation and involvement of broader neuronal circuits. Further studies are needed to clarify their mechanisms and clinical significance.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

papers.title: [Place the AEDs on the street! The circadian problem in the city of Pontevedra].
Utilization of Mental Health Resources and Self-Help Interventions Early on in Recovery Following Sexual Trauma.
papers.abstract: Early intervention in the trauma recovery process can be crucial in mitigating downstream negative mental (e.g., PTSD, depression) and physical health effects (e.g., somatic complaints, sleep disturbances, bodily pain). The extent of engagement in both self-help interventions and more formal mental health services in the early aftermath of sexual trauma is unknown. This study assessed the utilization rates of formal mental health services and informal self-help strategies (e.g., mindfulness, relaxation, physical activity, music and art, and yoga) of 169 sexual trauma survivors (Mage = 38.9 years old) over the course of eight weeks (T1 = withinone month of trauma, T2 = four weeks post-T1, T3 = eight weeks post-T1). Participants were recruited from an online survey platform. Within one month of a sexual trauma (T1), 23.7% engaged in mental health services and 92.3% engaged in at least one self-help strategy. At T2, 25.4% were utilizing mental health services and 95.3% were engaged in self-help strategies. At T3, 29.6% were using mental health services and 95.3% were engaged in self-help strategies. Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) was the most endorsed trauma-focused psychotherapy. The two most utilized self-help strategies were relaxation (e.g., progressive muscle relaxation, massage, deep breathing) and mindfulness/meditation. These findings suggest that many women turn toward self-directed coping strategies in the early aftermath of sexual trauma and fewer utilize mental health services. This study provides insight into early coping behaviors, highlighting future opportunities to expand self-help strategies as an understudied component of trauma recovery while decreasing barriers to access formal mental health treatment.

papers.title: Evaluation of Brain Activity in Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder Using Standardized Low Resolution Electromagnetic Tomographic Analyses (sLORETA).
papers.abstract: This study evaluated Default Mode Network (DMN) brain activity in females with Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD)/Dysphoric PMS and asymptomatic controls using archival quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG) and standardized low-resolution brain electromagnetic tomography (sLORETA) data. Eyes-closed resting-state EEG analyses were examined across follicular and luteal menstrual cycle phases. The analytic sample included 157 participants: PMDD/Dysphoric PMS (n = 87) and asymptomatic controls (n = 70). Nonparametric Wilcoxon Signed Rank Tests were used for follicular-to-luteal within-group comparisons, and Mood's Median Test was used for luteal-phase between-group analyses. Asymptomatic controls showed significant follicular-to-luteal mean-Z changes in cingulate gyrus delta, cingulate gyrus theta, and insula theta. PMDD/Dysphoric PMS participants showed a significant percentage-of-aberrant-voxels change in angular gyrus beta2. During the luteal phase, PMDD/Dysphoric PMS participants showed significantly higher subcallosal-gyrus beta2 mean-Z activity than asymptomatic controls. Luteal subcallosal-gyrus beta2 abnormal-voxel values were descriptively higher in PMDD/Dysphoric PMS participants (19.43%) than in asymptomatic controls (4.13%); however, this voxel-percentage comparison is reported descriptively because luteal-phase between-group percentage-of-voxels analyses did not reach the study threshold for statistical significance. These findings support further investigation of DMN-linked neural activity, subcallosal-gyrus beta2 activity, and phase-related network adaptability in PMDD.

papers.title: Adolescent Sleep Insufficiency and School Start Times: Why Public Health Must Lead.
Prevalence and Factors Associated With Falls in Individuals Aged 50 Years and Older Living in Urban and Rural Areas in Brazil: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.
papers.abstract: The factors associated with falls may differ from urban to rural areas. However, there is a paucity of studies investigating this topic. To investigate the prevalence and factors associated with falls in individuals aged 50 years and older living in urban and rural areas. This cross-sectional study analyzed 9402 participants aged 50 and older from the ELSI-Brasil study baseline in 2015-2016. Of these, 84.7% lived in urban areas. Self-reported falls in the last 12 months were assessed. The association of falls with age, sex, sleep quality, weakness, weight loss > 3 kg, slow gait, exhaustion, postural balance, osteoporosis, and depression was examined. Weighted prevalence estimates were calculated, and associations with falls were assessed using hierarchical Poisson regression models accounting for the complex sampling design and stratified by area of residence. The overall prevalence of falls was 22.4% and was higher among urban than rural residents (22.8% vs. 20.1%). Women had a higher prevalence of falls in both urban (PR: 1.64; 95% CI: 1.48-1.82) and rural areas (PR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.06-1.49). Compared with individuals aged 50-59 years, the prevalence of falls was higher among those aged 70-79 years (urban PR: 1.25; 95% CI: 1.10-1.43; rural PR: 1.54; 95% CI: 1.12-2.12) and aged ≥ 80 years (urban PR: 1.39; 95% CI: 1.17-1.66; rural PR: 1.65; 95% CI: 1.20-2.27). Slow gait (urban PR: 1.41; 95% CI: 1.22-1.63; rural PR: 1.67; 95% CI: 1.12-2.49) and exhaustion (urban PR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.29-1.65; rural PR: 1.93; 95% CI: 1.51-2.47) were associated with falls in both areas. Among urban residents, poor sleep quality (PR: 1.32; 95% CI: 1.20-1.44), weight loss more than 3 kg (PR: 1.23; 95% CI: 1.07-1.42), postural balance impairment (PR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.05-1.56), and depression (PR: 1.45; 95% CI: 1.28-1.64) were also associated with a higher prevalence of falls. However, significant interactions with area of residence were observed only for sex and depression. Over 20% of non-institutionalized Brazilians aged 50 years and older had one or more falls in the past 12 months. Female sex, older age, slow gait speed, and exhaustion were associated with falls in individuals aged 50 years or older in urban and rural areas. Poor sleep quality, weight loss > 3 kg, and depression were associated with falls only in individuals aged 50 years and older in urban areas. The association between female sex and falls was stronger among urban than rural residents, whereas the association between depression and falls differed significantly by area of residence and was observed only among urban residents. The ELSI-Brazil was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation-Minas Gerais and the process is registered on Plataforma Brasil (CAAE: 34649814.3.0000.5091).
papers.journal: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy

papers.title: Concordance Between Subjective and Actigraphy-Measured Sleep and Factors Associated With Discrepancies in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes.
papers.abstract: The relationship between sleep and glucose metabolism underscores the importance of evaluating sleep, especially given the high prevalence of sleep disturbances in individuals with Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Objective sleep measurements like actigraphy may not always align with subjective assessments, such as the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Although discrepancies between objectively measured sleep and subjectively measured sleep have been highlighted in healthy populations and other clinical populations, the relationship has not been well studied in individuals with T2D. We aimed to assess the discrepancies and correlations between actigraphy-measured and self-reported sleep parameters in individuals with T2D, and to identify demographic, psychological, and clinical factors contributing to these discrepancies. Adults (n = 134) with T2D wore actigraphy devices for 14 days and completed study surveys assessing subjective sleep (PSQI), demographics, and psychological and clinical factors. Findings indicated significant discrepancies in total sleep time (TST) and sleep efficiency between the two measurement methods, with self-reported TST being higher. Discrepancy levels varied by sex, depressive symptoms, and perceived stress. After adjusting for covariates, sex and depressive symptoms remained significant factors of greater discrepancies in TST and sleep efficiency. Age, marital status, housing stability, and sleep quality were also associated with discrepancies in sleep efficiency. Employment status and housing stability were factors associated with discrepancies in sleep midpoint. Discrepancies between subjective and objective sleep assessments suggest that integrating both methods could provide a more comprehensive understanding of sleep health. The findings also emphasize the need to consider individual psychological and demographic factors when interpreting sleep measurements.

papers.title: Associations of Serum Klotho and FGF23 Levels With Cognitive Function, Depressive Symptoms and Restless Legs Syndrome in Older Haemodialysis Patients.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment, depression, sleep disturbances and restless legs syndrome (RLS) are common among older haemodialysis patients, but the contribution of the FGF23-Klotho axis to these neuropsychiatric manifestations remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether serum FGF23 and Klotho concentrations are associated with these outcomes in this population. This prospective cross-sectional study included 89 patients aged ≥ 60 years undergoing maintenance haemodialysis. Serum FGF23 and Klotho concentrations were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Cognitive impairment was defined as Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) < 24 and depression as 30-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-30) ≥ 14; insomnia severity was assessed using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI; 0-28), and restless legs syndrome (RLS) was diagnosed according to the five essential revised International Restless Legs Syndrome Study Group (IRLSSG) criteria. Associations were evaluated using correlation and multivariable regression analyses, including Firth's penalized regression for RLS. Mean age was 71.3 ± 6.7 years; 58.4% were female. Cognitive impairment, depression and RLS were present in 52.8%, 40.4% and 13.5% of participants, respectively. Higher serum FGF23 was independently associated with cognitive impairment after adjustment for age, sex, educational attainment and dialysis vintage (OR per 1-SD increase = 5.46, 95% CI 1.18-25.36) and with RLS after adjustment for age and sex (OR per 1-SD increase = 2.31, 95% CI 1.21-4.42). These associations remained significant in sensitivity analyses. FGF23 correlated negatively with MMSE scores and remained associated with lower MMSE scores in adjusted analyses, whereas Klotho was not associated with cognitive measures. Neither biomarker was associated with depressive symptoms or insomnia severity. Higher FGF23 levels were associated with cognitive impairment, poorer cognitive performance and RLS in older haemodialysis patients, whereas serum Klotho was not associated with any of the neuropsychiatric outcomes examined; given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality.
papers.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society

papers.title: The Impact of Financial Toxicity on Mental Health of LGBTQ+ Cancer Caregivers in the United States.
papers.abstract: Financial toxicity and poor mental health are common among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and other non-cisgender heterosexual (LGBTQ+) cancer caregivers. This study aimed to assess the relationship between financial toxicity and mental health among LGBTQ+cancer caregivers. We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study (national survey and semi-structured interviews with a subset of survey participants). Data were collected from April 2024 through December 2024. Bivariate and multivariable regression models were used to examine the association between financial toxicity (modified COmprehensive Score for financial Toxicity [mCOST]) and mental health outcomes (Mental Health Continuum-SF [MHC-SF] and Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System [PROMIS] domains of anxiety, depression, sleep disturbance, and fatigue). A total of N = 316 LGBTQ+cancer caregivers participated in the survey, and N = 14 participated in an interview. Among caregivers, 34.5% reported high financial toxicity (mCOST< 22). The average MHC-SF score was 38.4 (SD: 16.9, range: 0-70). Mean PROMIS domain T-scores were: anxiety 59.7 (SD: 10.0, range: 40.3-81.6), depression 56.2 (SD: 10.6, range: 41.0-79.4), sleep disturbance 54.2 (SD: 9.2, range: 32-73.3), and fatigue 54.8 (SD: 11.9, range: 33.7-75.8). In controlled multivariable models, high financial toxicity was significantly associated with poorer mental health (lower MHC-SF scores [beta = -10.56, 95% CI: -14.47 to -6.65], and higher PROMIS anxiety [beta = 8.54, 95% CI: 6.33-10.74], depression [beta = 7.49, 95% CI: 5.07-9.91], sleep disturbance [beta = 6.33, 95% CI: 4.16-8.50], and fatigue [beta = 8.94, 95% CI: 6.26-11.63]. Qualitative analysis yielded two themes: (1) Financial Stress and Frustration and (2) Negative impacts of financial toxicity on health. LGBTQ+cancer caregivers experience high financial toxicity that is associated with poor mental health outcomes. Financial toxicity should be addressed in addition to general caregiving-related stress in this at-risk population.

papers.title: Time of day metabolism and endocrine regulation of immune health.
papers.abstract: The immune system is a dynamic, energy-dependent network regulated by temporal biology. Advances in circadian biology have enabled the synchronizing of critical immune parameters such as metabolism, endocrine secretions, surveillance, tissue repair, and adaptation to environmental cycles. Here, we propose a metabolomic, and endocrine, chromodynamic model of immune health, based on time-of-day rhythms. Immune resilience is defined by synchronization among three groups of oscillators i) the central circadian clocks, ii) food-entrainable metabolic oscillators, iii) peripheral cellular clocks. The model provides a framework to optimize these interconnected systems to maintain metabolic efficiency, minimize unnecessary inflammation, and enable precise immune responses through temporal gating. External factors of modern lifestyle disruptions, including irregular feeding patterns, sleep deprivation, and chronic stress, induce internal circadian desynchrony, contributing to persistent low-grade inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, immune aging, and chronic non-communicable diseases. We propose that immune health is characterized not merely by the absence of disease, but by stable circadian phase coherence, low inflammatory noise, and adaptive immune resilience. We have listed some chrono-biomarkers of metabolomic and endocrine parameters that may provide a functional assessment of immune resilience, defined by inflammatory tone, immune adaptability, metabolic integrity, and repair capacity. This framework integrates chronobiology, endocrine and immunometabolism to shift medicine from reactive disease management toward proactive assessment and restoration of biological resilience.

papers.title: Ticagrelor-Associated Central Sleep Apnea: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Implications for Sleep Medicine.
papers.abstract: Ticagrelor is a reversible P2Y12 receptor antagonist used for antiplatelet therapy and is well recognized to cause dyspnea. Emerging concern has focused on a possible association between ticagrelor and central sleep apnea, Cheyne-Stokes respiration, and other manifestations of ventilatory instability. This narrative review examines the clinical evidence for ticagrelor-associated central sleep apnea and the respiratory-control mechanisms proposed to underlie this association. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed, with Google Scholar and citation tracking used for supplementary discovery. Human clinical, physiologic, pharmacovigilance, and mechanistic evidence was synthesized qualitatively according to study design and evidentiary strength. Overall, the literature supports a possible association between ticagrelor exposure and central respiratory instability, although the incidence, clinical significance, and susceptibility factors remain uncertain. Enhanced ventilatory chemosensitivity and ventilatory overshoot provide a plausible physiologic framework, whereas equilibrative nucleoside transporter 1 inhibition and altered adenosine signaling remain proposed rather than established mechanisms in humans. Ticagrelor-associated central sleep apnea should therefore be regarded as an emerging medication-associated respiratory phenotype requiring cautious clinical interpretation. Prospective studies using standardized respiratory phenotyping, appropriate comparator groups, serial assessment, and clinically meaningful outcomes are needed to clarify susceptibility, reversibility, mechanisms, and clinical consequences.

papers.title: Insomnia severity and multidimensional psychological well-being in Chilean correctional personnel: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Prison officers in Chile work under highly stressful and dangerous conditions characterized by prison overcrowding, violence, long shifts, and chronic exposure to stress. Shift work and irregular schedules negatively affect sleep quality and contribute to insomnia, which in turn may impair psychological well-being. Despite growing evidence on occupational stress in correctional staff, limited research has examined the relationship between sleep quality, insomnia, and psychological well-being in prison guards. Therefore, this study aimed to assess working conditions, subjective sleep quality, insomnia severity, and psychological well-being among Chilean prison officers. A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted with 43 prison guards from five prisons in the Valparaíso Region, Chile. Instruments included the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), self-ratings of subjective sleep quality and the Ryff Psychological Wellbeing Scale (PWB). Sociodemographic and work-related variables were also analyzed, including sick leave, exposure to violence at work, need for mental health care, perceived organizational support, and energy drink consumption. Participants reported low institutional support (60.5%) and frequent sick leave (68.4%). Over one-third considered seeking psychological care (37.2%), and 53.5% reported daily energy drink consumption. Insomnia levels were moderate and clinically relevant (M = 17.87, SD = 0.91), with high dissatisfaction and functional impairment. Psychological well-being was moderate overall (M = 54.84, SD = 16.52), with higher scores in positive relationships and lower scores in environmental mastery and personal growth. No significant association was found between ISI scores and overall or subscale psychological well-being. However, insomnia was positively associated with years at the institution (p = 0.023, r = 0.349), indicating that longer tenure relates to higher subjective insomnia severity scores. Chilean prison officers exhibited clinically significant insomnia, moderate psychological well-being, and low perceived institutional support. Although no significant association was found between insomnia and psychological well-being, insomnia severity increased with years of service. These findings underscore the need to improve working conditions and implement policies that promote occupational health in Chilean prisons. Incorporating a gender perspective in this highly masculinized context is also recommended, as well as further research to enhance psychological well-being.

papers.title: Molecular origami in neuroscience: noncanonical DNA structures and functional nucleic acids in neural regulation and disease.
papers.abstract: Gliomas are increasingly recognized as network diseases in which aberrant interactions between tumor cells, neurons, and immune populations drive hyperexcitability, seizures, cognitive dysfunction, and disease progression. Simultaneously, advances in structural biology and nucleic acid engineering have revealed DNA to be a dynamic molecular architecture capable of sensing, regulating, and modulating cellular states. In this review, we examine how noncanonical DNA structures and functional nucleic acids including Z-DNA, G-quadruplexes, cruciform structures, aptamers, and DNA origami systems, shape neural regulation and glioma associated circuit pathology. We discuss how activity dependent DNA conformational transitions influence transcriptional programs controlling neurotransmission, ion channel expression, synaptic signaling, metabolism, and inflammatory pathways in glioma cells and peritumoral neural networks. Z-DNA formation appears linked to rapid transcriptional activation and enhancer dynamics, whereas G-quadruplex rich regulatory regions modulate genes associated with excitatory signaling, cellular proliferation, and tumor progression. Cruciform DNA structures additionally interface with genome stability and DNA repair, creating mechanistic entry points for therapeutic intervention. Beyond endogenous DNA architectures, we highlight the emergence of aptamer based diagnostics and therapeutics capable of detecting neurotransmitters, cytokines, and metabolites associated with glioma induced network dysfunction. DNA origami platforms further enable programmable multivalent delivery systems for targeted transport of small molecules, oligonucleotides, CRISPR machinery, and ion-channel modulators across the neurovascular unit and tumor microenvironment. We also explore closed-loop neuromodulatory strategies in which electrophysiological signatures guide state dependent therapeutic actuation through nucleic acid based sensing and delivery systems.
